Drop Site Daily: September 14, 2026 | | | Sep 14 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to reporters while aboard Air Force One while traveling back from Ireland to Joint Base Andrews, Maryland on September 13, 2026. Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images. Monday, September 14, 2026 -** Ansarallah advances toward Marib, captures strategic Red Sea islands, and launches attacks at Saudi air base. World Health Organization: Nearly 3,000 casualties, over 77,000 displaced in Yemen in one week. Over 2,000 Yemenis flee to Djibouti as clashes intensify. Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies role in attack on Saudi pipeline. Iran denies interference in Yemen, involvement in attack on Saudi pipeline. Reuters: Saudi Arabia has just seven days' worth of oil stored at Yanbu. Oil prices top $107 a barrel. U.S. officials meet with MBS, President Donald Trump claims talks with Ansarallah. One killed, four wounded in strike on Iranian vessel near Qeshm Island. Gulf-Iran meeting on Strait of Hormuz postponed at Saudi Arabia's request, Iran says. Iran nuclear chief barred from atomic conference after Austria denies visa. Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound more than a dozen across Gaza on Monday. Israeli soldiers and settlers continue to terrorize the occupied West Bank. Electricity generators failing at Gaza hospitals, Health Ministry says. Israeli forces raid Palestinian journalist home, beat son, order him to surrender. B'Tselem report documents Israel's "eliminationist project" in the occupied West Bank. Thirty-seven Palestinian journalists currently in Israeli detention, more than half without charge or trial. Israel continues to attack southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire" framework. EPA plans to eliminate greenhouse gas limits on power plants. AI chiefs call for slowdown in AI developments. Afghan resident deported after conceding to being an "alien terrorist" in first-of-its-kind case. NSA undergoes historic restructuring under Director Joshua Rudd. Rapid Support Forces drones strike Sudan's Ed Damazin amid fears of broader offensive. Scottish, Welsh, and Irish nationalist leaders declare right to self-determination at Cardiff summit. Trump calls for a unified Ireland. Syrians protest cost of energy, while Turkish Foreign Minister says Syria will play "vital role" in region's energy. Sweden's election too close to call as opposition edges ahead. 130 missing after passenger ship capsizes in Indonesia's Java Sea. Poland, Ukraine accuse Russia of "escalation" after strike near Boris Johnson. Ukrainian drones strike two Russian oil refineries as Trump tells Kyiv to stop "causing shortage of diesel fuel." Confirmed Ebola cases in DRC top 7,000. Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro faces corruption probe. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah advances toward Marib, captures strategic Red Sea islands: Ansarallah forces are advancing toward Saudi-backed government-held areas in Yemen, with fierce clashes reported on the outskirts of Marib, the government's strategic oil- and gas-rich stronghold, according to Al Jazeera. The group is also advancing in Taiz, where government forces are relying heavily on Saudi airstrikes to prevent the city's capture. Separately, Ansarallah captured the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands after hundreds of government-allied forces withdrew, AP reported. The islands lie about 160 kilometers north of Bab Al-Mandab in the southern Red Sea. The advances strengthen Ansarallah's position around Bab Al-Mandab--a key route for Saudi oil shipments amid the war with Iran and blockades in the Strait of Hormuz. Ansarallah launches attacks at Saudi air base: Ansarallah dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait in response to more than 300 Saudi airstrikes across Yemen over the past five days, military spokesperson Yahya Saree said Monday. Saree said the operation targeted fighter jet hangars, radars, runways, ammunition depots, and other military infrastructure, claiming "direct and precise" hits and significant damage. He warned that "any new aggression will be met with broader and more severe operations." Saudi Arabia's Civil Defense public warnings of potential danger in Khamis Mushait and nearby Abha three times early Monday. WHO: Nearly 3,000 casualties, over 77,000 displaced in Yemen in one week: At least 504 people were killed and 2,379 wounded across Yemen from September 6 to 12, to the World Health Organization. As of September 12, at least 77,789 people had also been displaced across Taiz, Marib, al-Jawf, Lahj, Hodeidah, Abyan, and Shabwa. Nearly half the casualties occurred in Marib, strategic Saudi-backed government-held governorate east of Sana'a. Separately, Yemen's Saudi-backed forces said more than 500 of their soldiers were killed and around 1,500 wounded in fighting with Ansarallah along the western coast from August 9 to September 10, while claiming more than 1,000 Ansarallah fighters were killed. The figures could not be independently verified. Over 2,000 Yemenis flee to Djibouti as clashes intensify: More than 2,000 Yemenis fleeing the fighting reached Djibouti, according to figures released Sunday by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). The number rose from around 1,400 arrivals reported a day earlier by Djibouti's Economy and Finance Minister. Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies role in attack on Saudi pipeline: The Islamic Resistance in Iraq responsibility for a drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline on Saturday, after the Iraqi government said the drones were launched from Iraqi territory. The group called responsibility for the attack "an honor we do not claim," criticized the Iraqi government for responding before completing an investigation, and offered to join an official inquiry. Iraqi security forces and seized a drone-launching platform allegedly used in the attack on the pipeline, according to the head of Iraq's Security Media Cell. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reshuffled military commanders in the country's border regions following the attack, dismissing the Maysan operations commander and provincial police chief. Iraq also temporarily three border crossings with Iran--Shalamcheh, al-Shib, and Mandali--after discovering drone launch sites. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Iran denies interference in Yemen, involvement in attack on Saudi pipeline: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei denied that Tehran interferes in Yemeni decision-making, saying Ansarallah is "an independent Yemeni party that takes decisions based on what it considers to be its own interests and priorities." Baghaei also rejected claims that Iran was involved in an attack on a Saudi oil pipeline from Iraqi territory, calling them "sheer lies" intended to deepen divisions among regional countries. Reuters: Saudi Arabia has just seven days ' worth of oil stored at Yanbu: Saudi Arabia has between five and seven days' worth of oil stored in its Red Sea port city of Yanbu, three unnamed sources told Reuters on Sunday, adding that Riyadh also has a smaller amount of oil stored in Egypt. Saudi Arabia said it suspended its East-West pipeline after the attack as a "precautionary measure." The shutdown of the pipeline, which allows exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, could threaten up to 4% of global oil supply. Oil prices top $107 a barrel: Oil prices rose more than 3% on Monday, with Brent crude futures gaining $3.21, or 3.1% percent, to reach $107.82 a barrel. U.S. officials meet with MBS, Trump claims talks with Ansarallah: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) met U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper and discussed the latest developments in the Gulf, Saudi state television reported on Monday. Trump, who spoke with MBS on Thursday and reportedly declined to intervene directly against Ansarallah, called MBS "a good friend of mine" when asked about their relationship on Saturday, and told reporters that "everything's going to work out fine and dandy." In the same remarks, he claimed that he had received a call from Ansarallah, who he said "don't want to fight" the U.S., and that they were "letting most ships go through" the Bab Al-Mandab strait. "There's one country they're not too happy with," he said, likely referring to Israel or Saudi Arabia, before promising to get the matter "straightened out." Iran One killed, four wounded in strike on Iranian vessel near Qeshm Island : One person was and four others were wounded, including two Pakistani citizens, after an Iranian cargo vessel came under attack near Qeshm Island early Sunday. Iranian state broadcaster IRIB, citing Qeshm's governor, said the vessel was attacked by the "U.S. terrorist enemy." Separately, a fire broke out on a commercial vessel struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday evening, forcing its crew to abandon ship, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations monitoring outfit. Gulf-Iran meeting on Strait of Hormuz postponed at Saudi Arabia 's request, Iran says: A planned meeting between Iran and Gulf states on the future of the Strait of Hormuz was postponed after Saudi Arabia requested a delay, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei, a claim Riyadh has yet to confirm. A regional official told AP that Saudi Arabia had proposed amendments over concerns the agreement could have lasting implications for other Gulf states. Baghaei called reported citing of the situation in Yemen a "flimsy pretext" and said an Iran-Oman agreement concerning the Strait had already been finalized. "Had this meeting taken place, it would have been a very suitable opportunity [to discuss the new policy]." Bahrain to participate in the meeting beforehand, arguing regional security "cannot be preserved through a policy of appeasement" and ruling out a collective meeting with Iran before their diplomatic ties were restored. Iran nuclear chief barred from atomic conference after Austria denies visa: Iranian nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami was unable to attend the International Atomic Energy Agency conference in Vienna after Austria denied him a visa. Iran's Foreign Ministry said Austria claimed it acted under U.S. pressure. Baghaei also dismissed about activity at Mount Kolang (Pickaxe Mountain) near Natanz as U.S. "media and psychological warfare." IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said there were "some indications" of activity at the site but acknowledged the agency had no "concrete information." IRGC claims downing of U.S. MQ-1 drone over Strait of Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Monday its Aerospace Force intercepted and downed an advanced U.S. MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, IRNA reported. South Korea, U.S. to discuss possible Korean military deployment to Strait of Hormuz: South Korea and the U.S. senior-level defense talks this week to discuss a possible South Korean military deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, Yonhap reported. South Korea last week sent a team to the UAE to assess the security situation near the strait. Iran and UAE sign joint BRICS statement calling for restraint in war: Iran and the United Arab Emirates signed a joint BRICS calling for restraint in the war. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian also met with Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi--the highest level meeting between the two countries since the start of the war. "We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in Middle East/West Asia [and] call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation," the joint BRICS declaration read. U.S. authorities claim Iran used Chinese satellite images in attack on Jordan base: Unnamed U.S. officials told the Wall Street Journal that they believe Iran obtained high-resolution satellite images from Chinese sources before Iran's July attack on Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti airbase that three American soldiers, calling it the "clearest" evidence yet of Chinese support for Tehran during the war. The unnamed officials declined to identify the specific Chinese entity involved and stopped short of directly accusing Beijing. Trump brushed aside the report, reporters on Sunday that, "they basically do what we do... when they say China spies on us, I say you're right, and we spy on them too." Asked whether he would raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping at their planned September 24 meeting, Trump reiterated that he has "a good relationship" with Xi and that "he's behaved reasonably well, and we behave reasonably well." A spokesperson for China's Foreign Ministry rejected the accusations as "groundless." Iran seizes property from 240 people accused of ties to Israel: Iranian authorities property belonging to 240 people accused of affiliations with Israel and other hostile countries, according to Iran Wire. The judiciary accused them of carrying out "propaganda or practical actions against the country" that caused extensive infrastructure damage. Under an expanded espionage law passed last year, assisting the U.S., Israel, or other hostile states can carry the death penalty. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 25 injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,786 killed, with 174,771 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,372 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,659, while 831 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian, wound more than a dozen across Gaza: Israeli forces a Palestinian in the Al-Mawasi area west of Rafah on Monday, according to WAFA. In Gaza City, an Israeli drone a tent sheltering displaced Palestinians, wounding more than 10 people, several seriously. In central Gaza, an Israeli drone struck a group of Palestinians near the Egyptian Committee headquarters in Al-Zawayda, leaving several wounded, some seriously. Another Israeli drone strike west of Khan Younis wounded several Palestinians, including one seriously. Israel continues to kill in Gaza throughout the weekend: Sunday: An Israeli strike targeted a vehicle in Gaza City's Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood, killing two Palestinians and wounding 13, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent. Drop Site contributor Abdel Qader Sabbah spoke to witnesses at the scene of the attack; one Palestinian man at the site held up household items in the car and asked, "Are these rockets? Are these guns?" Sabbah 's dispatch is available . Saturday: Israeli warplanes 13 Palestinians, including children, in two strikes near Khan Younis on Saturday, according to WAFA. Separately on Saturday, a pregnant woman and her unborn baby died from wounds sustained three days earlier from Israeli gunfire south of Khan Younis. Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed spoke to the victim's family. "We sit in fear. We sleep in fear. We walk in fear. Everything is fear," her mother-in-law told him. His video report is available. Israeli soldiers and settlers continue to terrorize the occupied West Bank: Ramallah: Israeli settlers with three bulldozers a road through olive-planted land west of Ni'lin on Monday for a new settlement outpost, WAFA reported. Hebron: Israeli forces a Palestinian after pursuing his vehicle in Beit Ula, then deliberately set the vehicle on fire. Tulkarm: Israeli special forces at the vehicle of Mohammed Shahada, 46, secretary of Fatah in Tulkarm refugee camp, before detaining him. On Sunday, medics received a 27-year-old Palestinian who had been shot in the foot by Israeli forces. Bethlehem: Israeli forces detained two children, aged 14 and 15, during a raid on Bethlehem on Sunday, WAFA reported. Separately, Israeli forces opened fire in the Kremzan area of Beit Jala, wounding two Palestinian workers en route to their workplace in Jerusalem. Jenin: Israeli forces shot and wounded two Palestinian farmers in the village of Fuqqu'a, according to Al Jazeera. Israeli soldiers reportedly opened fire after settlers let livestock loose on the Palestinian farmers' property and a group of Palestinians tried to stop them. Salfit: Israeli settlers two Palestinian men on agricultural land in Salfit on Sunday, severely injuring them. Tubas: Israeli forces five members of the Bani Odeh family from Tammun, south of Tubas, early Sunday, according to the Prisoners' Society in Tubas. The family members were detained as a means of pressuring another son to turn himself in to Israeli authorities, the Society reported. East Jerusalem: Israeli forces in the Silwan neighborhood in East Jerusalem on Saturday, moderately injuring a Palestinian man near the Al-Aqsa mosque. Electricity generators failing at Gaza hospitals, Health Ministry says: Several electricity generators at hospitals in the Gaza Strip are no longer working due to shortages of spare parts and fuel, the Strip's Health Ministry told Al Jazeera, noting the small quantities of fuel that Israel allows into Gaza were sufficient only for emergency needs. Read Mohanad El-Hemrwawi's report for Drop Site on the collapse of Gaza's strained network of generators . Israeli forces raid Palestinian journalist home, beat son, order him to surrender: Israeli forces the Jenin home of prominent Palestinian journalist Ali Al-Samoudi, beat his son Majd, and gave Al-Samoudi one hour to turn himself in. He was not home at the time. The raid comes months after Al-Samoudi was released in April 2026 after a year in Israeli detention without charge. He emerged having lost half his body weight--from 120 kg to 60. When Israeli forces arrested him, they broke down his door and beat him and his wife. He was held for 80 hours handcuffed and blindfolded and severely beaten on his way to Megiddo prison. Al-Samoudi was also shot while reporting alongside Al Jazeera journalist Shireen Abu Akleh during an Israeli raid on Jenin refugee camp in May 2022. Abu Akleh was killed by Israeli forces during that raid. B 'Tselem report documents Israel's "eliminationist project" in the occupied West Bank: The Israeli human rights organization B'Tselem released a lengthy new report entitled "The Elimination Project" on Monday, detailing Israel's "systematic effort to dismantle Palestinian collective existence in the West Bank." The report says this effort has accelerated since the current government took office in December 2022 and especially since October 7, 2023, identifying five interconnected mechanisms used by Israeli forces in the territory: violence and intimidation, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction, and ethnic cleansing and territorial takeover. Israel has established 200 new checkpoints since October 7, 2023, the report finds, seized about 18% of Palestinian land in the occupied West Bank through settlements and illegal outposts, and depopulated 64 Palestinian shepherding communities. B'Tselem's full report is available . 37 Palestinian journalists currently in Israeli detention, more than half without charge or trial: The Palestinian Prisoner's Society (PPS) on Sunday that 37 Palestinian journalists arrested since October 2023 remain in Israeli detention, more than half of them--19--held without charge or trial under administrative detention. Among them is Drop Site contributor Mohamed Awad, detained by the Israeli military from his home in Beitunia, near Ramallah, on August 12 and ordered to be held for four months without charge. The group also noted the case of female journalist Bushra al-Taweel, who was recently transferred to solitary confinement in Ramleh Prison, amid escalating repressive measures against female Palestinian prisoners. Palestinian prisoners ' rights group reports deteriorating health conditions at Ofer, Janot prisons: The Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs Sunday a deterioration in the health and humanitarian conditions at Israel's Ofer and Janot prisons. The group highlighted the case of 60-year-old Maher Naasan from Al-Mughayyir village, who was detained on July 6 and, according to testimonies from released prisoners, was severely beaten, had cigarettes extinguished on his body, and was held for hours under the sun. Palestinian prisoners at Ofer described outbreaks of scabies, insufficient cleaning supplies and clothing, cell raids, confiscation of belongings, and deliberate prevention of communal prayers by prison authorities. In Janot prison, the commission noted the case of Osama Fatahallah Al-Shenni, detained since 2024, who suffers from a herniated disc and has been denied painkillers despite severe pain, and has lost 35 kilograms since his detention. Trump defends Witkoff, Kushner work in Gaza, says Hamas ready to disarm : Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One, Trump the success of his Middle East envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, saying, "look at the fact that we got all of the hostages back." He also claimed that "there's not a lot of fighting in Gaza," and that Hamas "is now willing to give up their weapons." Israel has killed more than 1,370 Palestinians since the so-called ceasefire and has continued to push further into Gaza, occupying more of the Strip's land. Trump similar comments during his visit to Ireland on Saturday, saying that his administration had "put out the fire in Gaza" and calling their world "quite amazing." Israeli minister vows to revoke citizenship of filmmakers behind Gaza documentary: Israeli Culture Minister Miki Zohar said on Sunday that he would move "immediately" to revoke the citizenship of filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after their documentary "NAZA," about "Israel's calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza," won the Special Jury Prize at the Venice Film Festival. Zohar called the film "vile" and accused the pair of "treason against the state" in a on X. Netanyahu to visit U.S. from September 23-25: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is scheduled to visit New York City for the United Nations General Assembly, arriving in the U.S. on Wednesday, September 23 and leaving on Friday, September 25th, his office told the Times of Israel. He is expected to speak before the body on the 24th. Netanyahu has an outstanding arrest warrant issued against him by the International Criminal Court for war crimes and crimes against humanity for Israel's war on Gaza. Lebanon Israel continues to attack southern Lebanon despite "ceasefire" framework: Monday: Israeli forces heavy machine-gun fire toward the outskirts of Chaqra and Baraachit in the Bint Jbeil district, intimidating residents who had attempted to return to their homes, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Sunday: Israeli warplanes two strikes on Mansouri in the Tyre district, struck the outskirts of Haris in the Bint Jbeil district, and targeted an area between Mayfadoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqiya in the Nabatieh district. Lebanese President visits Nabatieh as talks with Israel postponed: Joseph Aoun, President of Lebanon, Nabatieh city on Saturday, surrounded by soldiers providing a military escort. Nearly 30 people have been killed in the southern Lebanese city since early September. The visit follows reports by Axios's Barak Ravid that talks between Lebanon and Israel scheduled to take place in Rome next week have been postponed to October. U.S. News EPA plans to eliminate greenhouse gas limits on power plants: The Trump administration to announce Monday that the U.S. will no longer regulate greenhouse gas emissions from power plants, according to the New York Times. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin is expected to announce the change during a G20 energy ministers meeting in Houston, arguing that greenhouse gases from power plants do not endanger human health or the environment and therefore fall outside the agency's authority under the Clean Air Act--a legal position that, if upheld by courts, could prevent future administrations from restoring such regulations. The Biden-era rule it replaces had been projected to generate $120 billion in public health benefits by 2047, including preventing up to 1,200 premature deaths and 360,000 asthma attacks annually by 2035. Social Security COLA projected at 3.6% for 2027: Government inflation data Friday points to a 3.6% Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for next year, according to an AARP forecast, which would mark the largest increase since 2023's 3.2% (this year's COLA was 2.8%). The official COLA, determined by averaging July, August, and September figures from the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, will be announced October 14. The adjustment will apply starting in January to benefits for 75.7 million Americans. Trump discusses interest rates ahead of Fed meeting: President Donald Trump Sunday in Ireland that the U.S. should have the lowest interest rates in the world "regardless of their formulas," even as data released Friday showed consumer prices rose more than expected in August, pushing traders to price in an 86% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month and two increases by year's end. When asked whether he expected the central bank to raise rates at its upcoming meeting, Trump said "I don't know," while suggesting Fed Chair Kevin Warsh 's hands may be tied by what Trump has called a "very political" board of governors. Trump also restated an earlier threat to cut off trade with countries the U.S. has a trade deficit with if the Fed doesn't lower rates, telling reporters "yeah, I'm going to do that with some nations" and that it "will take place over a period of time," though it remains unclear how such a move would influence Fed policy. AI chiefs call for slowdown in AI developments: The chief executive of artificial intelligence company Anthropic, Dario Amodei , published a 3,800-word open on Saturday calling for a slowdown in the development of A.I., with increased guardrails and oversight. The letter prompted the heads of other leading A.I. companies, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman , SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , and the chair of Google DeepMind Demis Hassabis , to speak out in agreement. In his letter, Amodei pointed to the hack of Hugging Face by hundreds of autonomous AI agents: "Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it's my worry that in 6-12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails," he wrote. President Donald Trump on Monday on Truth Social: "The only control or "guardrails" that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI 'people' from doing bad, or potentially bad, 'things,' like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a 'perfect little angel' \- and we will continue to do so!" He continued: "There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so." While AI executives call for new regulation, former FTC Chair Lina Khan that existing laws prohibit these companies from developing "dangerous, unvetted, or defective products" and enable the government to criminally prosecute those who violate them. OpenAI researchers have already produced models that have hacked different companies multiple times. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, by Khan's argument, could thus be tried for violating the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act under current U.S. code. Afghan resident deported after conceding to being an "alien terrorist" in first-of-its-kind case: Nazira Haji Zada, 47, an Afghan permanent resident living in Texas, to leave the United States rather than continue fighting her case in the Alien Terrorist Removal Court, the Justice Department announced Friday. The case was the first overseen by the secretive court, which was created in 1996 with the express intention of allowing the government to deport noncitizens using usually classified national security information. Its rules bar the accused from reviewing classified evidence against them or legally challenging how it was obtained. Haji Zada, who has never been charged with a crime, "conceded that she is an alien terrorist and waived appeal of the removal order," according to the department, which had alleged she worked to radicalize her son and son-in-law, both of whom were convicted over a plot to carry out an ISIS-inspired mass shooting on Election Day 2024. NSA undergoes historic restructuring under Director Joshua Rudd : The National Security Agency is set to its most extensive internal restructuring since 2016, creating five new organizations at its Fort Meade headquarters focused on artificial intelligence, China, cybersecurity, "warfighting" support, and global intelligence, according to current and former officials briefed on the plan and cited by The Washington Post. The initiative, spearheaded by NSA Director and Army General Joshua M. Rudd , will place each new division under a "mission director" holding effective deputy director-level authority, with candidates potentially drawn from outside the agency--a prospect one former official said has unnerved NSA insiders, noting the agency is "begging people to come back, especially leaders." The elite hacking unit Tailored Access Operations, reconstituted by Rudd and set for a significant budget increase in the new fiscal year, will fall under the global intelligence mission director. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News RSF drones strike Sudan 's Ed Damazin amid fears of broader offensive: Explosive-laden drones multiple areas across Ed Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile region, Sunday evening, with witnesses reporting at least 11 detonations near a military hospital and airport as army anti-aircraft guns fired to repel the attack, according to Sudan Tribune. The Sudanese Armed Forces also reported shooting down a drone that intended to strike the town of Balang, though Reuters could not independently verify this claim. The strikes come as the Rapid Support Forces have escalated drone deployment along the Blue Nile axis, which, in conjunction with reported troop mobilization, is believed by many locals to signal a broader ground offensive. Scottish, Welsh, and Irish nationalist leaders declare right to self-determination at Cardiff summit: Leaders of the Scottish Nationalist Party, the Welsh Party Plaid Cymru, and Northern Ireland's Sinn Fein their nations' right to choose whether to remain part of the UK at a rare joint meeting in Cardiff on Monday, signing a memorandum of understanding stating: "Our nations have the right to self-determination. No Westminster government has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future." The parties diverge on timing and method: the SNP wants a second independence referendum after Scotland's narrow 2014 vote to remain in the UK; Sinn Fein seeks a vote on Irish reunification; and Plaid Cymru favors independence only in the longer term, with no immediate referendum push. Trump calls for a unified Ireland: President Donald Trump during a Saturday meeting with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin in Dublin that he would "love to see [Ireland] unified," adding that he thought it eventually would be. The remarks put him at odds with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and drew criticism across party lines, including from his erstwhile ally Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. Burnham's office reaffirmed his unchanged position and commitment to the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill said Trump's comment showed "the unity debate is very much alive." Syrians protest cost of energy, while Turkish FM says Syria will play "vital role" in region's energy: On Sunday, protests erupted near Idlib, with footage circulating online showing residents blocking the Damascus-Aleppo international highway near Maarrat al-Nu'man, and additional demonstrations reported in Hama and Khan Sheikhoun. The protests center on the cost of energy, with the Syrian government having raised diesel prices by up to 40% and gasoline by 28% on Sunday. It described the increases as temporary and cited higher global fuel costs and an overhaul of its Baniyas refinery. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Sunday that, in light of Hormuz disruptions, Turkey would like Syria's overland connections "to be built not only on the map but also practically through railways, highways, and pipelines." Seven inmates killed in Kobane prison fire amid Kurdish protests over killing : At least seven inmates were and dozens injured, burned, or suffocated after a fire broke out during a prison riot in the predominantly Kurdish town of Kobane in northern Syria, state-run news agency SANA reported on Saturday. The riot, which the UK-based Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said began overnight after authorities decided to transfer some inmates to a facility in Aleppo, followed Friday protests over the killing of former Kurdish fighter Sami Sheikhmous Hiso, whose body was reportedly returned to Kobane bearing gunshot wounds after he was kidnapped. The Kobane prison remains under Kurdish administration and has not yet been transferred to the central government . Israeli military continues moves in southern Syria: The Israeli army expanded its incursion in the southern Syrian governorates of Rural Damascus, Quneitra and Deraa on Sunday, firing artillery rounds near Beit Jin before entering the village, and sending a separate patrol of four vehicles into the northern Quneitra countryside, Al Jazeera reported. Israeli soldiers reportedly set fires in the area before withdrawing. Sweden 's election too close to call as opposition edges ahead: Sweden's general election too close to call as of Sunday evening. The center-left Social Democratic opposition led 176 to 173 seats in the 349-seat parliament, with 94.4% of votes counted, according to the Swedish Election Authority. Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson told supporters "Sweden will get a new government" if results hold, though her party appeared headed for its worst showing in more than a century at 28.1% of the vote, down 2.2 percentage points from 2022. The nationalist Sweden Democrats, whose leader Jimmie Akesson said "we will not know tonight" who forms the next government, fell to third place with 17.6% support, down nearly 3 points from 2022. 130 missing after passenger ship capsizes in Indonesia 's Java Sea: At least six people and 130 remain missing after the passenger ship Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 passengers and crew, capsized in the Java Sea amid rough weather, according to Indonesia's search and rescue agency Basarna. The ship lost contact with its operator early Sunday while sailing from Surabaya to Banjarmasin. 107 people have been rescued so far. Poland, Ukraine accuse Russia of "escalation" after strike near Boris Johnson: Poland and Ukraine Russia of "escalation" after a strike hit a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train just two kilometers from the Polish border on Sunday, while former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and ex-CIA Director David Petraeus were at a nearby station in separate trains. No casualties were reported. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow "deliberately" struck the locomotive, while Polish President Donald Tusk warned on X that "the escalation of actions by the Russian Federation is becoming a fact" and flagged Russia's growing use of faster, harder-to-intercept jet-powered drones. Ukrainian drones strike two Russian oil refineries as Trump tells Kyiv to stop "causing shortage of diesel fuel": Ukrainian drones two Russian oil refineries with a combined processing capacity of roughly 400,000 barrels per day overnight into Sunday, according to Ukraine's General Staff and geolocated footage. Ukrainian drones struck the Slavyansk refinery in Krasnodar Krai, near occupied Crimea, and the TANECO refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, roughly 1,200 kilometers from Ukrainian-held territory. Russian officials said the Nizhnekamsk strike killed two civilians and wounded 14, after a drone hit near a parked car. President Trump publicly urged Kyiv to halt its refinery campaign. "He has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia," Trump said of Zelenskyy, "because he's causing a shortage of diesel fuel." Russia, meanwhile, launched 453 drones at Ukraine overnight, its largest barrage in weeks, striking Odessa for a second straight night, according to Ukraine's Armed Forces. Confirmed Ebola cases in DRC top 7,000: The number of Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 7,022, government data released on Friday showed. The government noted that the outbreak had spread to a seventh province, South Ubangi, located in the northwest of the country. Brazilian presidential candidate Fl avio Bolsonaro faces corruption probe: A Brazilian Supreme Court justice unsealed a into right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, just weeks ahead of the first-round vote on October 4. Flavio, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, is under investigation for receiving millions from Daniel Vorcaro, a banker arrested in March over fraud allegations, to finance a biopic about his father. Bolsonaro's main rival is President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva with polls showing a tight race. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241064%2E444211%2EHn_A6h)
I’ve been on the road since August 24th and plan to stay on it through Election Day. Visiting every major college campus throughout Texas to register Gen Z Texans to vote in the critical upcoming election.
Since August 24th I’ve been to Arlington, Denton, Stephenville, Dallas, El Paso, Austin, San Marcos, and San Antonio.
Today I’m in McAllen and I’ll be visiting Edinburg, Brownsville and College Station in the next few days.
At UT Austin, I met Joshua, one of the 1.2 million Texans put on the suspense list. We were able to get him back on the active list by confirming his voter registration at the correct address.
At Cedar Valley College I met Destiny, she just turned 18 which meant we were able to register her to vote and she’ll be voting this November in the most important election of her life and mine.
In Texas there’s no online voter registration, no automatic or same day registration and they’re constantly changing or closing polling locations where young people vote.
That’s why Powered by People volunteers show up where young people are, to meet them in person, make sure they’re registered and personally stay in touch with them until we confirm their ballot has been cast.
This is the work that works:
Every single donation will help keep me on the road and make sure our organizers have the resources to keep registering as many Texans as they can before the voter registration deadline on October 5th.

And right now, most polling in every swing state is a coin flip. Within the margin of error, either way. When it's that close, only one thing matters -- **_turnout._** Charlie Kirk built Turning Point Action to be the ballot-chasing machine that tips the scales in races like these. In 2024, we went 10 for 10. Every state we worked, President Trump won. **The formula is simple: Knock more doors. Chase more ballots. WIN more races. ** It's what Charlie called "the clipboard and tennis shoes" work to reach every voter. It's not glamorous, but... it's the work that wins. **And right now, Charlie 's machine is on the ground chasing ballots in Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire. ** If we win these states, we can lock the Left out of power for a decade -- if not for a full generation. _That 's why we're reaching out to you today... _ Every day, we're churning out new classes of trained ballot chasers to go door-to-door in these key states. | | | | Peter, For decades, bison have legally grazed on federal grasslands in Montana. But this winter, the Bureau of Land Management **suddenly reversed course, tore up the permits, and issued a formal eviction notice to nearly 1,000 bison on the prairie.** The administration suddenly decided that bison no longer count as "livestock" under the Taylor Grazing Act because they aren't being raised for "production-oriented purposes." Because this specific herd is managed for conservation and ecosystem health rather than maximum commercial slaughter, the government declared them ineligible to eat the grass. They want the bison hauled off so 63,000 acres of your public land can be handed over exclusively to commercial cattle operations. Here is why this matters to every single person who cares about the outdoors:
* This is a calculated move to establish that public lands exist _solely_ for private profit and corporate extraction.
* If they can arbitrarily ban the American bison—the literal, snorting symbol of the American West—from the prairie using a bureaucratic loophole, they can eliminate anything that stands in the way of a commercial lease.
* This policy shift was spearheaded by political appointees who were granted special ethics waivers to shape federal policy that directly benefits their former cattle industry clients.

We are not going to let them turn our prairies into a privatized feedlot. [**We are building a rapid-response war chest to expose this blatant overreach, fight back against the permit cancellations, and hold the politicians who engineered this purge accountable. | | Here in the South, now that the Supreme Court has greenlit racist new voting maps, we’re up against a full-on, coordinated, Neo-Confederate effort to rip representation away from Black and brown voters and cement one-party rule for the GOP. It’s a five-alarm fire. But Black leaders have warned that our region isn’t getting the resources and attention it needs: POLITICO:“Black lawmakers and activists across the Deep South argue they have been abandoned by the Democratic Party to fight an existential crisis on their own. They say they’ve been let down by nearly all corners of the party: would be-presidential hopefuls who have flocked to early and swing states but don’t bring their megaphones elsewhere; congressional leadership focused on majority-making battlegrounds while safe Black seats are drawn out; and years of chronic underfunding that has allowed local party apparatus to wither away.” [No matter what, Fair Fight will never abandon the South. _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3088%2E259176%2EtpEl1n) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3088%2E259176%2EtpEl1n)_

Folks,

I know I’ve been talking a lot on the campaign trail recently about the wonderful people who have come out to our town hall tour: teachers, farmers, nurses, retirees, Republicans and Democrats alike, who believe our state is ready for something better. But today, I’d like to talk about the one person we have not seen on the campaign trail: **Tommy Tuberville**.

I honestly can’t remember the last time Tuberville held a public campaign event in Alabama and answered questions from ordinary people. And I think there’s a reason for that. **He doesn’t believe he needs to listen to Alabamians to win this election**. I’d like to take a moment to tell you why, and what he plans to do instead.

Tuberville’s got a two-part plan to win this election.

**First, he’s going to do everything he can to make it harder for Alabamians to vote**. He’s already worked with our state government to rush through new maps which strip away Congressional representation from Black Alabamians. And right now, he’s working in Washington to pass the SAVE Act, a sweeping voter suppression bill which would end vote-by-mail as we know it.

**Second, Tuberville plans to buy this election through television ads**. He’s accumulated an _$8 million_ war chest that he’s preparing to dump into ads attacking me and spreading fear, division, and hate. For every day from now until November, Alabamians are going to be hearing Tuberville howl through their TVs about how communists and Muslims are coming for their families if they don’t vote for him.

You certainly won’t hear a thing from him about what Alabama’s government can actually do to help ordinary people. You won’t hear about saving our rural hospitals, abolishing the grocery tax, giving our teachers a raise, or lowering costs for working families. But I suppose when you have $8 million, you don’t have to.

**So let me tell you about my two-part plan to fight back.**

**First, we have to vigorously defend Alabamians’ right to vote.** We’ve got to support the fight against voter suppression in the courts and in our communities. We have to help Alabamians understand the rules, especially if Tuberville tries to push through any last-minute changes. And if Tuberville succeeds in getting rid of vote-by-mail, we have to make sure that elderly and disabled Alabamians can physically get to the polls.

**Second, we have to raise the resources to stand up to Tuberville’s massive war chest.** We cannot allow his lies, fear, and division to be the only things Alabamians hear about this election.

**[Tuberville thinks Alabama is for sale. Can you make a split donation between Blue Amp Action and my campaigns today to prove him wrong?](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16187?t=4&akid=3088%2E259176%2EtpEl1n)** | [DONATE $24 >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/16187?t=5&akid=3088%2E259176%2EtpEl1n)

clean_body: | It’s up to us to prove him wrong. You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates, If you'd like to unsubscribe, Folks, I know I’ve been talking a lot on the campaign trail recently about the wonderful people who have come out to our town hall tour: teachers, farmers, nurses, retirees, Republicans and Democrats alike, who believe our state is ready for something better. But today, I’d like to talk about the one person we have not seen on the campaign trail: Tommy Tuberville. I honestly can’t remember the last time Tuberville held a public campaign event in Alabama and answered questions from ordinary people. And I think there’s a reason for that. He doesn’t believe he needs to listen to Alabamians to win this election. I’d like to take a moment to tell you why, and what he plans to do instead. Tuberville’s got a two-part plan to win this election. First, he’s going to do everything he can to make it harder for Alabamians to vote. He’s already worked with our state government to rush through new maps which strip away Congressional representation from Black Alabamians. And right now, he’s working in Washington to pass the SAVE Act, a sweeping voter suppression bill which would end vote-by-mail as we know it. Second, Tuberville plans to buy this election through television ads. He’s accumulated an $8 million war chest that he’s preparing to dump into ads attacking me and spreading fear, division, and hate. For every day from now until November, Alabamians are going to be hearing Tuberville howl through their TVs about how communists and Muslims are coming for their families if they don’t vote for him. You certainly won’t hear a thing from him about what Alabama’s government can actually do to help ordinary people. You won’t hear about saving our rural hospitals, abolishing the grocery tax, giving our teachers a raise, or lowering costs for working families. But I suppose when you have $8 million, you don’t have to. So let me tell you about my two-part plan to fight back. First, we have to vigorously defend Alabamians’ right to vote. We’ve got to support the fight against voter suppression in the courts and in our communities. We have to help Alabamians understand the rules, especially if Tuberville tries to push through any last-minute changes. And if Tuberville succeeds in getting rid of vote-by-mail, we have to make sure that elderly and disabled Alabamians can physically get to the polls. Second, we have to raise the resources to stand up to Tuberville’s massive war chest. We cannot allow his lies, fear, and division to be the only things Alabamians hear about this election. | Thank you, Doug | We’re facing a critical moment in American history, which means what we do right now will define the future of our nation and our world. Peter — I know I ask you to chip in a lot. And I know there are things in your life that matter a whole lot more than a political campaign.
So I want to be clear about something:
[If giving today would make things harder for you or your family, please don’t.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
I mean that.
But if you are in a position to spare a few bucks, this is one of those moments when I could really use your help.
[Right now, this race is a coin flip.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
We’re in the final stretch, and every dollar we raise right now helps determine how many voters we can reach, how long we can keep our ads on the air, and how hard we can fight all the way through Election Day.
In a race this close, a whole lot of people doing something small can make a very big difference.
So, truly — only if you can swing it:
[$1](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.) — I’m with you.[$5](https://trk.email.vivekforohio._SqbA) — Let’s win Ohio.[$10](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-MMuFBHKy8CBg3dcnQ) — Put it where it helps most.[$25](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-_g) — Let’s keep pushing.
And if today’s not the day,[ $0 — I’m still with you](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.) is a perfectly good answer too.
I’m grateful you’re here whether you give $1, $25, or nothing at all. [But if you do have a few bucks to spare today, I promise we’ll put them to work:](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)

Thank you for being in my corner. It means a lot.
\- Vivek Ramaswamy

body:
| | | Peter, We're calling working-class voters in must-win congressional districts — and it’s never been easier for you to join the team! **Starting tonight, join us online any Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday night between now and Election Day to call voters and let them know how WFP champions will fight for them in Congress.** Whether you’re a first-time caller or a seasoned pro, our team will be there to provide you with training, a script, and tools for success, as well as answer any questions while you call. **[Click here to find a phone bank shift (or a few!) that works for your schedule, and make a difference in some of the country’s closest races.](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJxZAP5xLg1YZaKIinIFmIx_V8VfKqZfHylufhxygLW6EVIjaZpgqdwPmbLXckz7FLW7CXu2AJYnwKCCQQUF4nXep-dgRHzze0VD03CxpANC5PA205s6_55znkLxRrUBoMjxMvI05XvlhA-YpOnYk3Y4SRXmu8__RZQN7Yh9N8_ensYVHIqaxmeobN2IvfSe518--O0ueVZ_fKrz-M_moGhqnGpNMwG8-6xgg0pMdq3pZBrfMMIkojixbNU9gCU1KojKdBK5rRlz_XcGreeOo4j/4u1/3okk2njeQWSYPglzKxWNfg/h0/h001.-YXd3bWt7d4batpsz-T4joW62CCx0WhVzTkT77pNX00)** **[Join a phone bank](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMbGj-ca0TYSsYMZBvIweYdJxZAP5xLg1YZaKIinIFmIx_V8VfKqZfHylufhxygLW6EVIjaZpgqdwPmbLXckz7FLW7CXu2AJYnwKCCQQUF4nXAt70yMRLO1g2otkkePdPA4Fg_JprHyst3MhBJVdK4FHzuJKIjXKEiz2C5B7PckbDeMKAm6AFh9bBlh3iF6zqiGydaTtFX0KZaUrPGHXENNw-9n9QTPYtHdCfdUKKWKr_QFNUJ2XvGJgavA3qE-45opCfIcLQayAxiMenVTDN33UmsCG1xI_Z9VfkCIknytZW/4u1/3okk2njeQWSYPglzKxWNfg/h1/h001.MTbaRn-eq_ouXv86lfyNx9VSQ_CgZ0-yxi1jMQPit0g)** The battleground districts we’re calling will decide who controls Congress for the next two years of our fight against authoritarianism and for policies that work for working people. In primary elections across the country, we’ve seen Working Families champions beat dark money and sweep races by fighting for the policies that voters care about — bringing down skyrocketing prices, standing up to data centers, and more. We can keep that momentum going and win up and down the ballot. But to do that, we need to make sure voters in battleground districts know what our champions are fighting for and how they can make their voices heard this November. That’s where you come in. name: Roy Cooper
subject: I’m hoping there’s something I can tell you
body:
You have the power, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1330&source=&t=1&akid=3426%2E124072%2E_WPPCB) | | | |
---
Campaigns are tough, Peter.
There’s so much work to be done in so little time, and it’s all very expensive.
We set big fundraising goals for our campaign so that we can ramp up – not pull back on – the things that will help us win this election, but that means in the days leading up to our deadlines, **the pressure is on.**
[**_I’m hoping there’s something I can say to convince you to make your first donation today to help us hit our September mid-month goal before tomorrow at midnight._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1330&amount=5&t=8&akid=3426%2E124072%2E_WPPCB)
What if I told you that everyone from President Trump to Vice President Vance to Stephen Miller is personally attacking me and lying to voters about me and my values?
What if I told you that my Republican opponent dropped a seven-figure ad buy in North Carolina and a recent poll came out showing this race statistically tied?
What if I told you that GOP dark-money super PACs are pouring over $100 million into this race so far to halt our momentum – and Republicans say spending could reach up to $600 million?
**The GOP is coming after me so hard for one simple reason: If we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate.**
[**_You have the power to ensure that doesn’t happen. Please, Peter: Will you chip in $5 or even just a few bucks today to help us reach our critical $2.5 million mid-month goal, fight back against the GOP’s attacks and win this race?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1330&amount=5&t=9&akid=3426%2E124072%2E_WPPCB)

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

* [**Cait Conley is running in NY-17**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139182522/646511291/-1911020572?refcode=ga&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGRhMzY1NzAtNWViMC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=PutuVfwhCPamrWrhB57PvrS--Dky_-kUe4dItYziJ0c=): A fourth-generation Hudson Valley native and Army veteran, Cait served 16 years in the military, including six combat deployments.
* [**Bobby Pulido is running in TX-15**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139182523/646511292/-1911020572?refcode=ga&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGRhMzY1NzAtNWViMC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=PutuVfwhCPamrWrhB57PvrS--Dky_-kUe4dItYziJ0c=): Bobby is a Tejano musician and lifelong South Texan running for Congress in a newly drawn district.

Ten amazing candidates. Ten very distinct, American stories. One shared goal: to serve and make life more affordable and less chaotic. And a good snapshot of the House battlefield heading into the final stretch.

I’ll keep sharing more about the candidates and races on Red Alert as we get closer to Election Day.

Best,Gabe

# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2863%2E5691347%2ERKF73F)

Yesterday, Jon spoke to a massive crowd in Athens about the First Family’s corruption, his extreme MAGA opponent, and the importance of the midterms.
With only weeks to go before the polls open, we’re running out of time to get Jon’s message to every voter across Georgia. And it will take a massive amount of resources to reach the voters we need to win.
That’s why we have to ask: [**Can you chip in $5 to Jon’s reelection campaign today? Every donation counts when the stakes are this high.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-sep26.MEWcSy&refcode=em260914-1-subs&utm_campaign=em260914-1-subs&amount=5&t=2&akid=2863%2E5691347%2ERKF73F)

Here’s why this moment is so important:
At the end of this month, our team will be legally required to report how much we’ve raised and the number of donations we’ve received. Then, those numbers will be made public.

Jon Ossoff for Senate

Hey folks,
This one is infuriating. Pete Hegseth keeps facing questions about his judgment, his conduct, and his handling of the war in Iran--and the people around him are reportedly turning on him.
But this episode is about something bigger than one guy. It's about what happens when loyalty to Donald Trump becomes more important than competence, accountability, or the consequences for the rest of us.
* [**00:01:28**] Why Republicans had the power to stop Hegseth--and why they refused to use it.
* [**00:03:28**] The human cost of putting unqualified loyalists in positions with extraordinary power.
* [**00:05:26**] The reporting about Hegseth's wife, his decision-making, and why people inside Washington reportedly want him gone.
* [**00:08:36**] An old Hegseth clip about unlawful orders hits very differently now.
* [**00:10:41**] The bigger accountability crisis: Congress had chances to draw a line, and Republicans folded.

This isn't just palace intrigue about who's leaking on whom inside the Pentagon. It's about what happens when powerful institutions stop demanding competence and people become afraid to stand up to a president. We're talking about war, American service members, military readiness, accountability, and decisions that can affect millions of lives. Dear Fellow Virgin Islander,
My name is Lance Elliott Griffin, and I'm the Field Director at SaveVI.SaveVI is the first system built in the VI, for the VI, that puts the election in your hands.
**We have had almost three decades of failed one-party rule, which has led to widespread corruption, astronomical costs with WAPA, skyrocketing crime, failing schools, and unaffordable housing and healthcare.**
Political competition creates accountability and better government. Broader representation in the Virgin Islands Legislature would establish a line of communication with the White House and federal government.
Opposition would provide a check and bring new ideas and different ways of thinking to our Legislature, restoring balance so no party can take voters or power for granted.
We didn't build SaveVI for one politician. We built it because we were tired of watching our islands struggle while our people had no real power to change it. So we built the power ourselves.
---
| |
**This year, SaveVI is working to help Eric Tillett, Derrick Callwood, and Raymond James bring new leadership and accountability to the Virgin Islands Legislature.**
**Eric Tillett** is a St. Thomas businessman and entrepreneur running for Senate in the St. Thomas–St. John District. He brings years of experience building businesses and managing property, along with detailed plans for infrastructure, sewage and wastewater management, and government accountability.
**Derrick Callwood** is a former Virgin Islands police officer and St. Thomas businessman running for Senate in the St. Thomas–St. John District. His background in law enforcement and business gives him firsthand experience with the challenges facing the islands, with priorities including public safety, education, the cost of living, and accountability in government.
**Raymond James** is a lifelong Virgin Islander, small businessman, former Assistant Attorney General, and community advocate running for Senate in St. Croix. He is focused on restoring accountability and fiscal responsibility, putting public assets back to work, creating jobs, and expanding opportunity for Virgin Islanders.
---
| |
We need two types of people right now:
**COMMUNITY USERS** Regular Virgin Islanders who will use SaveVI 15–20 minutes a week to identify supporters. This is the heart of our movement. If you love the VI, this is for you.
**PAID FIELD REPS** Leaders who can recruit other field reps, actively persuade voters, and manage a team. This is paid organizing work for serious leaders who want to build something historic. You will be trained and paid to organize.
This is our life's work, and it only works if people like you step up and use it.
Ready to get to work? Tap the button below.
---
| [CHECK OUT SAVEVI.ORG](https://us.list-manage.com/DzAf8ZLMOXq?e=4f81ceec6f&c2id=39a671a1d75d16cde42206c3cb925b2d)
---
| |
For the Virgin Islands,
Lance Elliott Griffin Field Director, SaveVI616-437-6293

clean_body: A law with my name on it? The dubbed "Stop Nick Shirley Act" was made to stop me. | | | | | | | Friend, There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the "Stop Nick Shirley Act" means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law actually does. Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Friend: it makes it harder for anyone -- me included -- to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent. I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; this is just the beginning. Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General -- the one person in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Friend. That's the system protecting itself. I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't -- daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. They're right -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Friend: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, Lincoln Media Foundation was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. That 's why I'm partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation. They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the first place. I'm grateful for their partnership and commitment, and - helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them. Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer. Friend, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that's why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech -- and that's why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! # [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=881%2E127862%2EdRciGN)
We’ve got good news and bad news.
**The good news:** **A new independent poll recently dropped and showed us ahead of our opponent Joe Lombardo _for the first time_ in this campaign:**
**EMERSON | Nevada 2026 Poll**
🔵 Aaron Ford 44%
🔴 Joe Lombardo 42%
**[Can you chip in now to keep us in the lead as we head into the final 50 days of the campaign?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260914_1_ak.6TsRmx&amount=5&refcode=em20260914-881&t=3&akid=881%2E127862%2EdRciGN)**
Just last month, we were polling behind Lombardo. The energy on the ground is very real: as I continue to meet with folks across the state, it’s clear that **Nevadans are ready for change.**
**The bad news** is that we can’t take this new poll as a race already won. We have to keep up the momentum to stay in the lead. Our opponents will see this too — and they’ll do whatever it takes to stop us.
I’ve spent my career fighting for the Nevada family — taking on corporate landlords, cracking down on price gouging, and beating Trump's administration in court nearly 85% of the time. This will be a tough race, but I’ve never backed down from a fight, especially when it comes to making Nevada better for all of us.
**We’re showing that people-power can beat Lombardo’s special interest money. The momentum is on our side — and we need to increase our efforts now more than ever.**
**[This poll is just the start — we have 50 days to make it a reality on Election Day. Can you chip in $5 or more to help us reach even more voters and win in November?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20260914_1_ak.6TsRmx&amount=5&refcode=em20260914-881&t=4&akid=881%2E127862%2EdRciGN)**

Thank you,
Aaron

The Democrats laid out their target list for winning back control of the US House - but we're not taking that lying down. For the good of the country, we're going on offense. Jay Feely (AZ-01): A former professional football kicker and strong Trump ally, Jay will fight to keep our border secure, deport illegal aliens, and kick the Swamp into shape. Kevin Lincoln (CA-13): A Mayor, pastor, and Marine who served the President of the United States on Marine One, Kevin has dedicated his life to serving his community and country. Joe Mitchell (IA-02): A non-profit leader who also worked under President Trump's Administration, Joe will fight to protect our farmers and end the Democrats' reckless spending. Paul LePage (ME-02): A two-time elected Governor of Maine whose American Dream story began sleeping in horse stables after becoming homeless at 11, Paul will end wasteful Democrat spending and bring back American jobs. Laurie Buckhout (NC-01): A retired Army Colonel and decorated combat commander from a long line of combat veterans, Laurie will fight to support our Veterans and make sure they receive the care they deserve when their mission is complete. Mike LiPetri (NY-03): A Conservative former New York State Assemblyman and champion of law enforcement, Mike will fight the pro-crime Democrats and help dismantle gangs trafficking fentanyl into our communities. Peter Oberacker (NY-19): A successful businessman from the Hudson Valley, Peter will fight to win this critical swing district and focus on bringing down the costs of groceries, utilities, and gas. Tano Tijerina (TX-28): A born and raised South Texan, Tano learned the importance of faith, family, and hard work. As a county judge, Tano locked away hardened criminals and will continue to fight to support law enforcement and the American Dream. Eric Flores (TX-34): A US Army Veteran, Eric will be a champion for our veterans, fight to keep the border secure, and put a stop to migrant crime in our communities. Greg Cunningham (NM-02): A Marine Veteran and law enforcement officer, Greg will fight for law enforcement, bring down the costs of energy, and keep the Southern border secure. John Braun (WA-03): A retired Navy Captain and job-creating manufacturer, John will fight to create more American jobs. Eric Conroy (OH-01): An Air Force Captain Veteran who answered the call when the Twin Towers fell on 9/11, Eric will fight for working families and revitalize Main Street America. Jim Desmond (CA-48): A Navy Veteran and commercial pilot, Jim will fight to lower costs and deliver safer communities. Brinker Harding (NE-02): An Omaha business leader, Brinker will rein in wasteful spending in Washington and work to reduce the National debt. Marty O'Donnell (NV-03): An award-winning composer for television shows, movies, and video games, Marty will fight to keep our border secure and invest in American technology. Carrie Buck (NV-01): A Nevada State Senator and education leader, Carrie will protect parents' rights, defend no tax on tips, and fully fund law enforcement. Aaron Flint (MT-01): A decorated combat veteran and fifth-generation Montanan and radio host, Aaron will fight to bring back American manufacturing and make the American Dream affordable again. Barb Regnitz (IN-01): A successful business leader and long-time community volunteer, Barb will fight for law enforcement, safe cities, and secure elections. Mike Bouchard, Jr. (MI-10): A US Army Captain Veteran, Bronze Star recipient, and third-generation Michigander, Mike will fight to bring back American manufacturing and finish the border wall. Anthony DiLorenzo (NH-01): A father, successful business owner, and job creator, Anthony will fight to bring down costs, balance the federal budget, and protect our northern and southern borders. Jeanine Driscoll (NY-04): A mother of five children and practicing attorney, Jeanine will fight to lower taxes, support law enforcement, and protect no tax on tips. Derek Merrin (OH-09): A battle-tested conservative in the Ohio legislature who expanded school choice and played a key role in requiring a photo ID to vote, Derek will fight to bring housing costs down and secure our elections. Carlos De La Cruz (TX-35): An Air Force Veteran and small businessman with deep San Antonio roots, Carlos will fight to eliminate the cartels at the southern border and make sure our children inherit a country where God, Country, and Families can prosper. They’re joining every other major election forecaster in recognizing that the momentum is on our side. They know what we know: We are going to win this race.

**Alaskans are ready for change. I’ve spent the past nine months traveling to communities in every corner of the state – from Prince of Wales to St. Lawrence Island, the Kenai to the Arctic. And everywhere I go, I hear the same thing: Enough.**

Enough of Dan Sullivan’s self-dealing. He’s tripled his personal wealth since getting to DC, and Alaskans are paying the price. We are getting crushed by corporate greed while he turns the other way, and we’re tired of it.

I’m angry that the millionaires and billionaires have rigged the system in DC against working Alaskans. I’m angry that it doesn’t work for us anymore. But I’m also optimistic. Alaskans are can-do people. And together, on November 3rd, we’re going to take the first step toward taking back our state.

We won nearly 50% of the vote in our open primary election last month, against 15 other candidates of all parties – including incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan.

More than 82,000 Alaskans cast their ballots in favor of our fish, family, freedom campaign for a more abundant Alaska. We beat the incumbent by more than 8 points, and in the first poll of the general election, we’re leading Dan Sullivan by 1 point in the final round of ranked choice voting.

Because while Alaskans are sending a clear message that we’re done with the self-dealing politics of the past, we’re going up against the entire DC establishment and their billionaire-backed super PACs – and they are pummeling us with attack ads. They’re noticing the momentum that we’re building in Alaska, and they’re spending BIG to stop us.

That’s why this race is so close. It’s the closest race in the country, a true 50/50 toss-up! And while I feel confident that, in the end, we are going to win, it isn’t going to be an easy fight. We are up against a corrupt DC system, and they’re fighting with everything they have to keep it that way.

As one of the most engaged supporters of my U.S. Senate campaign in North Carolina, your involvement has had a real impact on our ability to stay competitive in this fight. Thank you.
I hope you know how grateful I am for your time and attention - **[and today, I 'm asking you to take the next step with a contribution of $5](https://substack.com/redirect/a2f90afc-27c3-4115-8f8a-87f5c31b6d46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).** Here's why:
Experts say Senate control will be decided in North Carolina, so between now and November, keeping up our momentum day by day is key to our success.
However, grassroots donations have fallen significantly and my finance team has had to make the tough decision to lower our projections for September.
That's a big problem when recent polling shows that this race is statistically tied, and when the Senate GOP's top super PAC has gone live with false attack ads against me.
If we have to make the massive budget cuts we're currently deliberating, we'll put our chances of flipping this seat at risk.
**[I 'm asking you to chip in and help us make today our biggest fundraising day of the month yet so we can turn things around before our mid-month deadline tomorrow night. I'd be grateful for your $5 or anything you can spare. It all adds up quickly when thousands of folks like you pitch in. Will you please donate?](https://substack.com/redirect/a2f90afc-27c3-4115-8f8a-87f5c31b6d46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Again, thank you.

# [Trump slams AI slowdown as a gift to China](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
President Donald Trump on Sunday **[waved off calls to slow artificial intelligence,](https://substack.com/redirect/41752d7b-32e3-4c17-9a5a-b2138043aea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/41752d7b-32e3-4c17-9a5a-b2138043aea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)telling reporters the technology will be "more good than bad, but by a lot."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Whoever wins, wins:** Speaking at the Amgen Irish Open in Doonbeg, Trump said, "Whoever wins AI, and we're leading by a lot. Whoever wins AI wins." He demurred on whether he uses AI.
* **Not downplaying the risk:** Asked if he had heard directly from AI leaders, he said he was "not downplaying" the harms and that he had "said it from the very beginning."
* **Amodei asked for brakes:** The remarks came days after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's Saturday essay urging a blanket slowdown to ensure safety.
* **Chips and a China lead:** Amodei pressed tighter limits on AI chips sent to Beijing and argued a Chinese lead would pose grave danger for the United States and the world.

# [Ellison scraps $7.5B Oracle sale. Shares still fall 4%](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison **[canceled a plan to sell up to 50 million shares](https://substack.com/redirect/47db395a-9c7e-4450-95df-61cedfcec7c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** worth $7.5 billion one day after it was disclosed, and shares fell 3.9% Monday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Weekend 10b5-1 reversal:** Ellison **[adopted the Rule 10b5-1 plan on June 22](https://substack.com/redirect/25f4a616-023e-4731-8467-0029b4ee8489?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to run through Oct. 24. Oracle disclosed it Friday and said Saturday he canceled it, with no shares sold.
* **Founder keeps control:** The 82-year-old still controls more than 40% of Oracle. Forbes had him above $400 billion a year ago; Bloomberg listed $204 billion and seventh on Sept. 13.
* **AI build weighs stock:** Oracle stock is down roughly 23% this year amid a heavy AI-infrastructure debt load, with single-quarter capex at $28 billion and free cash flow of −$5 billion.
* **Hollywood bid still stalled:** He is the **[father of Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison](https://substack.com/redirect/c8f4275b-c8ad-4307-8461-e5c93fe9fd1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and a backer of the proposed Warner Bros. Discovery purchase, now held up by a state attorneys general antitrust lawsuit.

* * *

# [Beijing: Amodei's AI slowdown is a Cold War playbook](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
China's Foreign Ministry on Monday **[dismissed U.S. AI executives' call to slow development](https://substack.com/redirect/a8a9150b-fc08-4687-a57c-59d4296f096b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as "fear mongering," as SoftBank sank 10% in Japan and AI-linked stocks slumped.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Guo draws the line:** Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said fear mongering, confrontation, and competition "will just disrupt [the] process of global AI governance," answering a question about Amodei, Altman, and Musk.
* **Security minister speeds up:** Minister of State Security Chen Yixin wrote Sunday that China should accelerate an AI security risk prevention system, calling AI the "main battleground" for technological competition.
* **Pacing has a ceiling:** Amodei's Saturday essay said building too fast is reckless, but slowing more than the U.S. lead over "CCP-associated projects" would create national security risk.
* **Xi works the other track:** At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, President Xi Jinping said China will take the lead in fostering AI collaboration among developing countries.
