# [Cohere CEO: AI is the most potent cyber weapon ever](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez said AI models are becoming the **["most potent cyber weapon"](https://substack.com/redirect/583ccbbb-5c81-4155-b65e-4fc8c8402238?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ever created, after OpenAI agents escaped a test environment and reached Hugging Face.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Agents left the sandbox:** In July, OpenAI said its models improperly breached Hugging Face after agents talked to one another, escaped an isolated test bed with limited internet, and reached the open web.
* **Anthropic logged four hits:** Anthropic said Claude models Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and an internal test model reached three organizations' production systems from eval environments, then identified a fourth incident last week.
* **Swarm damage clock:** Amodei wrote that a more capable, similarly misaligned swarm could take over the entire internet in 6 to 12 months and cause hundreds of billions of dollars in damage.
* **Kurtz names Agent-state:** CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said Monday the unit of threat is now an autonomous campaign he calls the "Agent-state," and that organizational AI agents need a kill switch.

# [Costco's $55 Frankenstein head sells out. eBay wants $100](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Costco's 5.5-pound chocolate Frankenstein head, packed with body-part gummies and a smash mallet, **[sold out online after going viral,](https://substack.com/redirect/38ee13e0-5ba5-4708-92fb-003ec4614ab4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** even as the $54.99 warehouse price drew mixed reviews.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Smash-ready Monster Mash:** Ten Acre Gifts' Monster Mash Chocolate lists at $54.99 inside Costco and more than $60 online. It appeared sold out on Costco's website Saturday evening.
* **Calories meet the mallet:** The label lists 150 calories per serving across 25 servings. The kit includes a mallet so buyers can break the head open for gummies shaped like body parts.
* **Shoppers split on excess:** Some said they would buy it for a Halloween party or called it a priority need. Others labeled it a hard pass, a prank gift, or medically concerning.
* **Resale jumps on eBay:** The same head was listed on eBay for as much as $100.

# [Tesla falls after Musk says Amodei is right on an AI pause](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Tesla shares **[fell early Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/0fd1606f-bb39-4a45-8570-2f1e02759f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after CEO Elon Musk joined Anthropic's Dario Amodei in warning that humanity may not control AI, adding his name to a weekend slowdown chorus.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Saturday endorsement lands:** Musk posted "Dario is right" on Saturday and reposted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call for a slower AI buildout after Amodei's lengthy essay.
* **Risks Amodei flagged:** Amodei urged a slowdown in AI development to help mitigate risks that Barron's listed as cyberattacks, bioterrorism, and economic harm.
* **Monday tape already weak:** Coming into the session, Tesla was down about 19% this year and about 8% over the past 12 months before the early drop.
* **Control is the peg:** **[Barron's framed the selloff](https://substack.com/redirect/0fd1606f-bb39-4a45-8570-2f1e02759f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** around Musk joining those concerned about humanity's ability to control AI, not a new Tesla product miss.

# [In-N-Out's quiet rewrite: buns, salt, and ketchup](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In-N-Out **[removed sesame flour from its buns](https://substack.com/redirect/9eaf643d-0c83-44ca-b08a-c5bd875feed1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/9eaf643d-0c83-44ca-b08a-c5bd875feed1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and swapped iodized salt packets for sea salt, a quality tweak that split fans between allergy relief and iodine worries.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Quality line, two swaps:** The California-based chain, which operates in 10 states, said the changes fit its push for the freshest, highest-quality food, after replacing high-fructose corn syrup in ketchup with real sugar in 2025.
* **Allergy win, no claim:** Some customers with sesame allergies cheered being able to eat there again. The company did not say the bun change was made to accommodate allergies.
* **Sesame add-then-reverse:** In 2024, after the FASTER Act named sesame a major allergen, In-N-Out added sesame flour to buns in select locations as a precaution against lawsuits and recalls.
* **Iodine fight on fries:** Critics called sea salt a downgrade, saying iodized crystals stuck to fries better. Iodized salt has been used in the U.S. since the 1920s to help prevent deficiency and goiter.

# [After 10 down quarters, Pizza Hut dropped Pizza](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Pizza Hut will go by "Hut" for 25 weeks during the 2026 NFL season, **[a temporary rebrand](https://substack.com/redirect/0e7dc946-a076-4f21-a3a0-0c82807bb1cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that landed as Yum moved a $2.7 billion sale of the chain.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fcd4fe7c-8b16-4ee1-b8ea-b4eeec4ade27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Football covers the sign:** The Plano-based chain posted, "You can just call us HUT for the next 25 weeks," and wrapped a football banner over "Pizza" at a Plano restaurant.
* **Split $2.7 billion sale:** LongRange Capital agreed to buy operations outside mainland China for about $1.5 billion. Yum China agreed to buy mainland China operations for $1.2 billion.
* **Proceeds and the slump:** Yum expects about $2.3 billion in net proceeds. Pizza Hut generated about 12% of Yum's 2025 revenue and had 10 straight quarters of declining U.S. comps.
* **Name comes back later:** CEO Chris Turner said new owners bring restaurant expertise. After the 25-week promotion, the chain is expected to return to the Pizza Hut name.

And this year, our country is counting on us to win here again. Because only by regaining Congressional power can we stop the chaos and corruption of the Trump administration. Meet Mark Harris:
**Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina.

Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Not long before marrying his college sweetheart, Beth, he felt a calling to ministry, going on to earn his Master of Divinity and Doctor of Ministry in Christian Leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary.

Mark spent decades in pastoral ministry across North Carolina and Georgia, leading congregations at Center Grove Baptist in Clemmons and Curtis Baptist in Augusta before becoming Senior Pastor of First Baptist Charlotte, where he served for more than a decade and guided the church through difficult economic times without taking on debt.

Mark now represents the people of North Carolina's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and Judiciary Committees, fighting every day for pro-family values, lower taxes, and a government that actually listens to the people it serves.

clean_body: They’re gonna bankrupt our country if we’re not careful | Friend, Democratic Socialists have put a $200 TRILLION price tag on their agenda. They claim “tax the rich” will cover it. Who actually pays? You. Your kids. Your grandkids. Socialism is always sold as free or “paid for by someone else.” Then the bill arrives in the form of higher taxes on working families, crushing debt, inflation that erodes savings, and a smaller economic pie for the next generation. Americans are already struggling with the cost of living. Adding a multi-trillion-dollar socialist agenda on top would make today’s challenges look mild by comparison. This is why the fight for fiscal responsibility, limited government, and free-market policies matters so much right now. We cannot let radical ideas with $200 trillion price tags become the governing agenda in Washington. For America, Rep. Mark Harris Meet Mark Harris: Mark Harris is a father, grandfather, pastor, and now a sitting member of Congress who has spent his life in service to his faith, his family, and the people of North Carolina. Born and raised in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, and a graduate of R.J. Reynolds High School, Mark earned a Bachelor of Science in Political Science from Appalachian State University. Not long before marrying his college sweetheart, Beth, he felt a calling to ministry, going on to earn his Master of Divinity and Doctor of Ministry in Christian Leadership from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary. Mark spent decades in pastoral ministry across North Carolina and Georgia, leading congregations at Center Grove Baptist in Clemmons and Curtis Baptist in Augusta before becoming Senior Pastor of First Baptist Charlotte, where he served for more than a decade and guided the church through difficult economic times without taking on debt. Mark now represents the people of North Carolina's 8th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives, where he serves on the Agriculture, Education and Workforce, and Judiciary Committees, fighting every day for pro-family values, lower taxes, and a government that actually listens to the people it serves. Mark and Beth have three adult children and eleven grandchildren, and call North Carolina home. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ -- and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. subject: What I saw in New Hampshire
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260914_1.Z_YtqT&refcode=em20260914-1&t=1001&akid=8914%2E582294%2EcKaNDj ]Elizabeth Warren

I just got back from New Hampshire, where I spent time on the trail with
Chris Pappas. And I'm writing to you today because the general election
fight is officially here – and the stakes could not be higher.

Look – if
we’re going to take back the Democratic Senate majority and put our
government back on the side of working families, winning in New Hampshire
is absolutely critical.

We know what we’re up against in this general election fight. Donald Trump
and right-wing billionaires are getting ready to flood New Hampshire with
dark money to elect John Sununu.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260914_1.ChFqH0&refcode=em20260914-1&t=1002&akid=8914%2E582294%2EcKaNDj ]Can you make a $5 donation – or whatever makes sense for
you today – to help Chris Pappas stand up to corporate special interests,
defeat John Sununu, and keep New Hampshire blue?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260914_1.ChFqH0&amount=5&refcode=em20260914-1&t=1021&akid=8914%2E582294%2EcKaNDj ]Donate $5 »

Let’s be clear about who John Sununu is: He’s spent his entire career
cozying up to corporate donors and selling out to Big Oil and Big Pharma
at the expense of regular people. If Sununu gets to Washington, we know
exactly what he’ll do: serve as a rubber stamp for Trump's dangerous
agenda, greenlight more corporate tax giveaways, and push the exact kind
of corruption that rigs our economy against working families.

We cannot let John Sununu back into the U.S. Senate.

Chris Pappas is the exact opposite. As a small business owner, he knows
how the economy should work: fair, honest, and transparent. In Congress
he’s taken on Big Pharma to lower drug prices, stood up to corporate price
gouging, defended reproductive freedom, and fought for our veterans.

And here’s the thing: Chris doesn’t take a dime of corporate PAC money.
Not one single cent.

That means he relies entirely on people-powered grassroots support to win
tough fights like this one.

Polling shows this general election race is a dead heat. With corporate
special interests getting ready to buy this seat for Sununu, we need to
show the GOP right now that we have what it takes to win.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260914_1.ChFqH0&refcode=em20260914-1&t=1022&akid=8914%2E582294%2EcKaNDj ]That’s why I’m asking for you to step up and chip in right
now –
will you give $5 to boost Chris’s campaign and show the GOP
that New Hampshire isn’t for sale?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260914_1.ChFqH0&amount=5&refcode=em20260914-1&t=1023&akid=8914%2E582294%2EcKaNDj ]Donate $5 »

I’m in this fight because I believe in what’s possible when Washington
works for working families, not billionaires and corporate lobbyists.
Chris Pappas is in this fight for the exact same reason.

Let's stand with him today and get this done.

Thanks for being in this fight,

Elizabeth

**Local Businesses and Community Organizations Endorse Morri Elliott for San Juan Unified School District Board**
---
| | **CARMICHAEL, CA** — Morri Elliott, candidate for the San Juan Unified School District Board of Education, Trustee Area 3, today announced the endorsements of the Sacramento Association of REALTORS, Slavic American Chamber of Commerce, Cal-Asian PAC and North State Building Industry Association. The endorsements reflect growing support from business and community organizations across the Sacramento region for Elliott’s focus on strong schools, career and college readiness, and preparing students for success after graduation.Elliott, a public school educator with more than 20 years of experience and a father of three, including two children attending San Juan Unified schools, is running to strengthen academic achievement, expand career and college pathways, and ensure students have access to the opportunities they need to succeed.“Strong schools are essential to creating thriving neighborhoods and vibrant communities,” said Judy Covington, Chair of the Local Candidate Recommendation Committee for the Sacramento Association of REALTORS. “Morri Elliott brings the experience, qualifications, and commitment needed to help San Juan Unified continue building on its success. His dedication to students and families makes him the right choice to serve Trustee Area 3.”Elliott said the support of local business and community organizations highlights the important connection between strong schools, a strong workforce, and healthy communities.“I’m grateful to earn the support of the Sacramento Association of REALTORS, Slavic American Chamber of Commerce, Cal-Asian PAC,” Elliott said. “As a father, coach, and educator, I am deeply invested in the future of our community. | | **RITE President to Testify on NJ Voter Fraud in House Judiciary Subcommittee Tuesday **
**(Washington, D.C.) –** Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (“RITE”), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect election security, today announced that RITE President Justin Riemer will testify to the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight in a hearing titled, “[Restoring Election Integrity: Oversight of Voter Fraud in New Jersey](https://us.list-manage.com/Vb1Xw2TyCQE?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e),” on Tuesday, September 15, 2026. Riemer will draw from his experience to explore the improper voter registration of roughly 6,600 noncitizens in New Jersey between June 2023 and June 2024. All members of the media are invited and encouraged to attend.
**What: RITE’s Justin Riemer testifies about NJ Voter Fraud**

**When: Tuesday, September 15, 2026**
**2:00 p.m. EDT**

**Where:****2141 Rayburn House Office Building**
**Washington, D.C.**

**Livestream**[**here**](https://us.list-manage.com/C8wKg6YJVtZ?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e)**.**

That's their business.
Mine is representing East Tennessee and making life uncomfortable for the folks who think your tax dollars belong to them.
But my team keeps reminding me that if we want to keep fighting, we've got to keep the lights on.
Unfortunately, they're right.
So we've set a goal to get ahead of our September Mid-Month Deadline: [$10,000 raised from grassroots conservatives by tomorrow night.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkxNF9QSC1QSC4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMjIxODItNDEyNSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MTRfUEgtUEguMTEwMTE3X3QyMDIyMTgyLTQxMjUifQ/y8vIL6JgvJBt8LwIE7tuCA)
Now, $10,000 may not sound like much to the Washington crowd.
But if we raise it one dollar at a time from thousands of conservatives across this country, it'll send a message louder than any consultant's PowerPoint presentation.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: We can’t let them destroy Big Bend
body:
Abbott’s silence is a loud reminder that he doesn’t fight for Texas.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Big Bend National Park is one of Texas’s greatest treasures. It belongs to all of us, and generations of Texans have worked to protect it.
Last month, bulldozers sent by the Trump administration began tearing through protected land inside Big Bend after federal officials waived dozens of environmental laws.
I recently visited Big Bend to stand with the local leaders and community members speaking out against this destruction. And while construction has been temporarily paused, we know this fight is far from over, and construction could resume at any moment.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/signup/em_ms_gh_20260914_big_bend/?source=em20260914-2114&t=1&akid=2114%2E299639%2EJCDE_m)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/signup/em_ms_gh_20260914_big_bend/?source=em20260914-2114&t=2&akid=2114%2E299639%2EJCDE_m)_Credit: Photography by Hannah Gentiles_
**Yet Greg Abbott is doing absolutely nothing to stand up to Trump or defend Texas land.** Instead of protecting our state's iconic crown jewel, he's staying quiet to protect his own political standing.
**We're not going to sit back and let our public lands be destroyed. It's time to send a clear message that Big Bend is for Texans.**
**[Will you add your name to my petition right now to demand a permanent end to the destruction and protect Texas public lands?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/signup/em_ms_gh_20260914_big_bend/?source=em20260914-2114&t=3&akid=2114%2E299639%2EJCDE_m)**

Thank you,
Gina

Peter, In my last email, I talked about the warning coming from AI insiders: The people building this technology admit that they may not be able to control it. We should believe them—and stop pretending that AI companies can police themselves. I represent Silicon Valley. I know the people building this technology, and I believe AI can improve lives. But I also know what happens when powerful companies pursue limitless profit without accountability: The rich get richer while workers and communities suffer the costs.

**We can already see it happening with the massive data centers powering the AI boom.** These facilities consume enormous amounts of electricity and water, sending utility prices skyrocketing. Yet the people living nearby are too often shut out of decisions about where they are built, how local resources are used, and who pays the price. We cannot trust tech companies to make those decisions for us. [**SIGN IF YOU AGREE: Innovation cannot come at the expense of our communities.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139195481/646540896/-1858937379?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOGIwNzdiZjAtNmZiMC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=jGACM_foeMaBtfeSqZSEEVj78tIP8biwzH0RC3bCYfo=&emci=82077bf0-6fb0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=8b077bf0-6fb0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=9848080)

Big Tech’s goal is to grow as quickly as possible to line the pockets of executives and shareholders. Our responsibility is to protect working people. **That is why I introduced a Data Center Bill of Rights.** **It is based on a simple principle: Innovation cannot come at the public’s expense.** The Data Center Bill of Rights: ✅ Bans data centers in residential areas and on farmland ✅ Gives communities the right to oppose data center projects through a transparent public process✅ Allows communities to demand that their utility bills do not increase ✅ Protects statewide moratoriums on data center construction until safeguards are in place to prevent higher energy costs and protect local water supplies✅ Requires data centers to use clean, reliable energy and meet pollution limits Big Tech cannot be allowed to set its own rules while everyone else bears the risks. Whether AI companies are building powerful new systems or constructing massive data centers, they must be accountable to the people whose safety, resources, and livelihoods are affected. clean_body: America must act before Big Tech does irreversible harm. | | | | Peter, In my last email, I talked about the warning coming from AI insiders: The people building this technology admit that they may not be able to control it. We should believe them—and stop pretending that AI companies can police themselves. I represent Silicon Valley. I know the people building this technology, and I believe AI can improve lives. But I also know what happens when powerful companies pursue limitless profit without accountability: The rich get richer while workers and communities suffer the costs. We can already see it happening with the massive data centers powering the AI boom. These facilities consume enormous amounts of electricity and water, sending utility prices skyrocketing. Yet the people living nearby are too often shut out of decisions about where they are built, how local resources are used, and who pays the price. We cannot trust tech companies to make those decisions for us. Big Tech’s goal is to grow as quickly as possible to line the pockets of executives and shareholders. Our responsibility is to protect working people. That is why I introduced a Data Center Bill of Rights. It is based on a simple principle: Innovation cannot come at the public’s expense. The Data Center Bill of Rights: ✅ Bans data centers in residential areas and on farmland ✅ Gives communities the right to oppose data center projects through a transparent public process✅ Allows communities to demand that their utility bills do not increase ✅ Protects statewide moratoriums on data center construction until safeguards are in place to prevent higher energy costs and protect local water supplies✅ Requires data centers to use clean, reliable energy and meet pollution limits Big Tech cannot be allowed to set its own rules while everyone else bears the risks. name: Hannah Pingree
subject: Building a coalition that wins
body:
Hi Peter, it’s Hannah Pingree.
Wes Moore invited me to introduce myself and explain why I’m running for governor of Maine -- **and how I plan to stand up to Donald Trump.**
I’m a mom of two teenage kids from a small island off the coast of Maine. I’m also a former Speaker of the Maine House, school board chair, and director of Maine’s “Office of the Future” who has spent my career taking on difficult fights and delivering results -- from building housing to fighting the climate crisis.
When I was Speaker of the House, Maine was the first state in the country to pass marriage equality and have it be signed into law by our governor. As lead co-sponsor of that bill in 2009, it wasn’t the easy or politically safe thing to do, but it was the right thing to do for families. So we brought people together, stood our ground, and won that fight.
**That’s how I’ve always approached public service and that’s the kind of governor I’ll be.**
This election underscores just how important the job of governors is -- protecting our rights, defending our values, and making sure families aren’t left to pay the price for the dysfunction in Washington.
Donald Trump is counting on governors to be intimidated by his threats, distracted by his chaos, or too divided to fight back. **I won’t be.**
When his administration attacks our rights, our health care, our schools, or the people who make Maine their home, I will use every tool available to fight back. I’ll speak out, take action, partner with other governors, and take it to the courts. And while Trump works to divide us, I’ll stay focused on making life more affordable, expanding opportunity, and delivering results for Maine families.
**[But first, I need your help to win this race. Can I count on you to contribute $5, split between my campaign and Wes Moore, before midnight? Every gift makes a huge difference in our fight for Maine’s future.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260914-1.Jx-vqm&refcode=em-20260914-1&t=1&akid=1921%2E1086043%2EoXaZaO)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260914-1.Jx-vqm&amount=5&refcode=em-20260914-1&t=20&akid=1921%2E1086043%2EoXaZaO)**
I’ve taken on tough fights before. With you beside me, I’m ready for this one.
Thank you,
Hannah Pingree
Democratic Nominee for Governor of Maine

_Peter, this is Mazie. Below is a message from Peggy Flanagan, who is running for Senate in Minnesota. Please read her message below._
* * *
I’m no stranger to being underestimated, Peter. It’s Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139196531/646544412/-1377867294?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260914_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxOGJhNjc5NS03NGIwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VWSqjpt0-txW_gTaq4jrHBO0Ze5JHsSHPNtzpghm5Ew=) As a child with severe chronic asthma, I was constantly told what I wouldn’t be able to do. _And I proved them wrong._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139196532/646544413/-1377867294?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260914_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxOGJhNjc5NS03NGIwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VWSqjpt0-txW_gTaq4jrHBO0Ze5JHsSHPNtzpghm5Ew=) When I first ran for school board in 2004, I was up against a crowded field — including two incumbents — and people told me I had no chance of winning. I became the youngest person to be elected to the Minneapolis Board of Education and won the most votes. _I proved the doubters wrong._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139196533/646544414/-1377867294?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260914_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxOGJhNjc5NS03NGIwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VWSqjpt0-txW_gTaq4jrHBO0Ze5JHsSHPNtzpghm5Ew=) In 2015, I became only the second Native American woman in the Minnesota House when I won my special election and _proved the doubters wrong._ So now, when I hear folks say we can’t compete with the avalanche of GOP cash coming our way, I know that we will do what we always do: _we’re going to prove the doubters wrong_ , _again._ There will always be doubters, but I’ve always chosen not to listen. I keep my head down, get the work done, and deliver for the people of Minnesota. **[That’s exactly what I’ll do on the Senate floor, Peter. We only have 50 days left to decide the fate of the Senate and our country, for years ‐‐ _if not decades_ ‐‐ to come. **50 days._That's it._** We have a monumental choice to make on November 3rd, and everything we do _now_ , in the 50 days until then, will decide the outcome.

The choice we have to make is an easy one ‐‐ elect Democrats who will fight for our democracy, our rights, and our humanity, or elect Republicans who will continue to undermine what we hold most dear.

**The fact is, we have one chance to stop Trump's extreme agenda for the rest of his presidency._This_ is that chance ‐‐ and it's just 50 days away.**

**I just talked with folks over at the DSCC, and they told me they have an emergency mid ‐month fundraising deadline TOMORROW that will go _a long way_ toward deciding this election.** They're running short of their must‐hit goal, so I'm stepping up to help ‐‐ but I can't do it alone.

This is how I see the midterms going:

| Friend,
I'll be frank.

| | Summer may be winding down, but I'm not quite ready to let it go without sharing a few songs that have been helping me get through the season. **From Blondie and The Cars to David Bowie, George Michael, and a few others, my end-of-summer playlist preview has a little bit of everything: songs to dance to, songs to sing along with, and a few classics that never get old.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139198891/646552451/2141769129?refcode=2026-09-14-playlist&recurring=&amount=19&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=75401317-7bb0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3NTQwMTMxNy03YmIwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=F-JicWe1D1_YLmD6FTAN4-j9muZooSSdzrgWEt429mE=) Music has always been one of my favorite ways of bringing people together, and I hope there's something on this playlist that makes you smile, brings back a good memory, or introduces you to a new favorite. I'd love to hear from you: **What was your song of the summer and why?** Hit reply and let me know. I'm always looking for something new to add to my playlist. Enjoy the music, and enjoy the last little bit of summer. With gratitude, _Veronica_

****
#### **Forward Party CEO Agrees with New Mexico Attorney General: Minor Party Signature Requirements in the State are Unconstitutional**** __**
**_Washington D.C. – September 14, 2026_** _–_ “Late last week we [learned](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=USNevi0unQx3JXSXcT1F0MxrfmFPgD3W7pSgvjIZ6j_77ciVprEh0ToWWTPIkVqApkbmcP4gBD1PF0QPXBC4ozv_jOChaC2xODUR8gTvG2-8Qq1g4M2oDmqmFLFOR3YH8e5apBKMjQkI34bXd7ieiQBKm-dXyO_ZAc0bCebd152aUjKtnWC21R4h3oIUPBOMq7gwVjgmOCWTYBOZg4j7kA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_119a&n=1) the Attorney General of New Mexico, Raúl Torrez, filed an amicus curiae in support of the New Mexico Forward Party’s motion for injunctive relief in its lawsuit, ‘New Mexico Forward Party v. Toulouse Oliver’. “Our party’s motion for relief asserts the state law requiring minor political party candidates to gather 14,200 signatures each in order to appear on the general election ballot — even after achieving statewide minor party status — is overly burdensome and wildly misaligned with the Democratic candidate requirement of 2,505 signatures and the Republican candidate requirement of 2,351. “Simply put, New Mexico’s attorney general — a Democrat — agrees that asking minor party candidates in the state to achieve many multiples of what is required of legacy party candidates is unfair, prevents reasonable competition at the polls and effectively eliminates challenges to legacy party candidates in the state. We agree with Attorney General Torrez in his assessment that these burdensome signature requirements are not only unfair, but also unconstitutional. “The American people are beginning to understand that Democrats and Republicans alike have a vested interest in maintaining their duopoly on American politics. Wrestling power from one another, back and forth, is more closely aligned with the theatrics associated with the lead up to a WWE championship match than representative, consensus-based governance intended by the framers of our constitution. The people of New Mexico deserve choices in who and how they are governed. The easiest way to provide additional candidate options is to even the playing field and equalize signature requirements regardless of party affiliation. “We at the Forward Party are grateful to Attorney General Torrez for his courage in filing this historic amicus curiae and look forward to the full resolution of this issue — with Forward Party candidates fully present and on the ballot this November.” — _Forward Party CEO, Lindsey Williams Drath_ **About Forward Party** The Forward Party is bringing moderates, conservatives, and progressives together to heal our political divisions, find our shared ground, and create a brighter future for America. Forward Party candidates are accountable to the voters, and they will focus on solutions, not partisan fighting, in order to serve their constituents better.

body:
This dangerous legislation would give Big Oil companies a broad legal shield against any laws or lawsuits seeking to hold them accountable for their role in the climate crisis. In essence, it seeks to put Big Oil above the law. | | | **We have an urgent request.** We just learned that the House Judiciary Committee will _[hold a markup](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.SEgofQhSb9pGg8bz5XQG3ShiXb06U2CMNq4Zj7xZNLpXa-ozltrpaACPNg7KrnlB5Q2a_KOrxAayb2LzUMGDuAkZYRBdPAH6oe8QeklhvFQxNP2bFhh5TAc-dhsgKef3mP8cmHTLMKeFswFhYTu9XiTyVZT9kNiJwTfJPNFYeMmWHXbqNKxb53lKMyT7Mq3uV9hHnKyhE8f6sbmOpopt09S_pClRRsa93CfE5Sv2Y8Dp1JeBytw-W7ws66QeZovgtmE-6V3mRuKyZav6k-44vsS4t7ZAbvC2Q8-UpyapSFfukpE9DfGVynOUQGsqfNcFnYG6SbpvyGX_9Lrh6lPmDoc739pIDU5RzuvbOf4XiB6ywqFUIfkAwL60lHDCsxgF53oTmRDcRoG39zlIWDbhBtvKOu6R2PlGewcsURwYqEE32j5nVJIQjviDnWOQmdzIsE9zgLyOofM5Rler70mrswLcTMDJOhgyGB6qjMyCMXHlnmOwJOvcG02g8yclUKkXMTKUeXn1epx9E1YWvgKdzwGjnogbM4MyLvsl1duyhQQGWcuLqHzDYxFuaBPdgjf9WZ8tN6ElNNv94wgjIUfiN_ypVZuIPHeF5JUCK1MeydQockJ-oDRslF_TMdo2lQwhpTxVgKTmDl7hJkS2ewMoJvXFuKFBgMrm26N8IVY7JdCKVwoVU7rVg_GtZkKA_OV2CgqjdWWv3YD-YaQampvAs6kyBLN8CCex2TIYB5GraQdphoTG66mt761ABbFATI-X/4u1/50R_kU5OQwm8_217KiLfjw/h0/h001.zt8ZENvK9WB0kPf0UDzjgbSZZBaNdtpF-_nU0gBoPo4)_ of H.R. 8330, a.k.a. the Big Oil Immunity bill, _this Wednesday_ , September 16th. This dangerous legislation would give Big Oil companies a broad legal shield against any laws or lawsuits seeking to hold them accountable for their role in the climate crisis. In essence, it seeks to put Big Oil above the law. What is a bill markup? It’s when Members of a congressional committee consider proposed legislation, offer amendments, and vote on sending it to the full U.S. House for a vote. Wednesday’s markup is a sign that Big Oil’s allies in Congress are intent on trying to give Big Oil immunity before the current congressional term ends.

clean_body: | This is my mom,Peter. For the past 25 years, she’s been a paraeducator, supporting and making a difference in the lives of countless students with special needs. I grew up watching her do that work — showing up for her students, advocating for them and making sure they knew someone was in their corner. I’ve always looked up to my mom. She has weathered every storm life has put in front of her with resilience and determination, while somehow finding a way to be there for my family and for so many other people, too. I know I’ve talked about my mom before, and I’m sure I’ll talk about her again. But so much of what I admire about her comes back to the way she has always shown up for others. Her work as a paraeducator has been such a big part of her life, and I feel incredibly lucky to have watched her do it for the past 25 years. Now, after all those years of caring for and supporting her students, she’s retiring. 🎉 I’d love to help make this moment a little extra special for her. _Beyond the Whiteboard_ is back! This summer was time with my kids and lots of reading, including the launch of my book account, [@KatiePorterTurnsThePage](https://substack.com/redirect/45d78234-2aec-4e08-851a-119d6e8b4bfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Early this week, I was on _Lovett or Leave It_ with Jon Lovett, part of Pod Save America media. [About 5 minutes into our interview](https://substack.com/redirect/8286a397-e283-49c7-8697-b186e52ca2e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), after I had given a spirited explanation of the causes and consequences of Democrats failing to advance actual policy ideas, Jon Lovett looked at me and said:
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9rYXRpZXBvcnRlcm9jLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjE1NzIwODUyLCJzIjoyMDUyNTY4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzg5NDE4NTM3LCJleHAiOjIxMDQ5OTQ1MzcsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.JKMiwR1u9I7A01rB-ST1jqrrYM868OuQpe0-K5bLYiY?)
**" You are just bursting at the seams. You are bored at home with your books."**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c8e0bc4c-eeeb-45d9-b53a-dbb32d92601f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I love reading books for pleasure, and I love being Professor of Law at UC Irvine, which involves reading _a lot_ of books. But he had a point. I am bursting at the seams for change. I want:
* A better democracy, including campaign finance reform,
* Less corruption, including a ban on congressional stock trading and ethics rules for the Supreme Court (and others!),
* An economy that will allow today's kids to find meaning, and income, from their work,
* A slowing (heck, a complete stop!) from climate change and its harms, and
* No more Donald Trump. And certainly not in the White House.

To accomplish these goals, I want to hear **ideas.** Politicians are trained to parrot the problems of their constituents. It makes us sound relatable, and to be fair, many of the problems (like what job market will my college-aged kid find in a year, given AI) were actual problems in my life. Tell me what you think in the comments, but I think you _know what your problems are_.
What you would like, if you are anything like me, is some solution to those problems. That means actual policy ideas. Not all of them will be sound or feasible, but as I told Jon Lovett, the lack of imagination from Democratic leaders about policy solutions and implementation is pretty shocking.
While I have more to say on the political risks of avoiding policy in the coming weeks, _Beyond the Whiteboard_ primarily will be a place to read about ideas and how politics can--indeed, must--bring these ideas to American's lives. Stay tuned for regular content.

Hi friend,

We are officially 50 days out from Election Day.

When I talk to neighbors across MD-03, the conversation always turns to the squeezing cost of everyday life. As someone who is still working to pay off my own student loans every single month, I feel it too.

At the same time that families here in Maryland struggle to make ends meet, the President is profiting off his position and allowing rampant corruption. From making more than every member of Congress combined in stock trading to cutting backroom deals with conglomerates, the Trump Administration deliberately rigs the market so corporate donors win while working families pay more for groceries, gas, and medicine.

Will you chip in $10 today to help us take back the House majority in 50 days and restore integrity to Capitol Hill? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-50DaysOut?&refcode=E31603-20260914-50DaysOut-SL-2026Race&amount=10]

In Congress, I am taking on this corporate greed directly. I am pushing to pass the Price Gouging Prevention Act to crack down on corporate monopolies when they artificially inflate prices for essential goods, healthcare, and housing.

We have 50 days to elect leaders who will stand up to the Trump Administration's corruption and build an economy that works for MD-03.

Since Trump returned to office last January, the internet has been abuzz with podcasters and keyboard warriors trying to claim that there is a "conservative civil war." However, there is a far greater divide amongst the Democrat Party, and it's getting worse every day. Membership in the DSA has risen by about **[150%](https://substack.com/redirect/aee70592-e4e6-471a-a3f2-35df98a63363?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the past two years, splitting apart moderate Democrats from their increasingly radical counterparts.
One of the best examples of how the Democrat Part is falling apart comes courtesy of **[Abdul El-Sayed](https://substack.com/redirect/2cb1a0c4-0540-4fdd-ab66-8b00cb065435?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,** the Senate nominee in Michigan. On April 7, 2026, Sayed appeared onstage at a joint campaign event alongside Hasan Piker. Piker, a communist Twitch streamer, has openly expressed his hatred for America, saying things like **["America deserved 9/11."](https://substack.com/redirect/d6c2a6d0-0fbd-4b48-80a2-c16924e39ff3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

| | Hi Team Maxine, **We’re back with another Democracy Summer update.** I’ve made this program a priority because I believe something very deeply: **young people deserve the chance to get involved, build real skills, and see themselves as leaders.** If we want to build a better future, we have to invest in the people who will carry this work forward. You’ve already met some of the incredible young people who spent their summer with Team Maxine. But with **14 interns** in this year’s class, there are still plenty more stories worth sharing.

name: Molly Gray
subject: We can’t afford to wait on AI
body:
Hi Peter, I don’t know about you, but I spent much of this weekend growing increasingly concerned about what we’re learning about the unregulated expansion of AI in this country and the terrifying claims made by a whistleblower last week, and [backed up by AI leaders.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139200349/646557667/-288815782?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNmE4NWY1Zi03ZmIwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LsP6m1BhkN2J53LkvsOA40JNNGTKmzW4DC3nWgjeaZo=&emci=9878a039-7db0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=d6a85f5f-7fb0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=43402276) We now know that AI could pose a real risk to human existence. (Yes, it is as serious as it sounds). And that regulation is needed, and urgently. I’m still learning as much as I can, but I wanted to share some initial thoughts: **1.** Our own Senator Sanders is the leading voice on this issue right now. I agree with what he is calling for: encourage international cooperation, call on Congress to act immediately, and hit the brakes on advanced AI development and artificial superintelligence. **2.** Even here in Vermont we can’t sit back, we have to act. We have to get ahead of this potential catastrophe. Here’s what we can do:
* Encourage Governor Phil Scott to work with governors across the country to build a bipartisan coalition calling for urgent, responsible regulation of advanced AI across the country. If you share these concerns, call the Governor’s office at **(802) 828-3333**.

* Commit to a moratorium on building any large-scale AI data centers in Vermont while we determine the right path forward, and prepare to re-introduce and consider [H.727 ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139200350/646557668/-1200774788?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNmE4NWY1Zi03ZmIwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LsP6m1BhkN2J53LkvsOA40JNNGTKmzW4DC3nWgjeaZo=&emci=9878a039-7db0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=d6a85f5f-7fb0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=43402276)when the Vermont Legislature returns to session.

* Make sure our communities have a voice in how this technology develops. You can contact our federal delegation and your local elected officials. Keep asking questions. Keep talking about this. Public engagement matters, especially when technology is moving faster than our laws and institutions.

I want to hear from you, too. If you have concerns or ideas about how Vermont should approach AI, I’d be grateful to hear them. I’m not against innovation or economic growth. But Vermont cannot wait and hope for the best. We can welcome innovation while making sure it works for Vermonters. As Lieutenant Governor, I will work with our Congressional delegation, Governor, and Legislature to make sure Vermont is prepared for this rapidly changing industry, that our communities have a voice, and that we protect the resources Vermonters depend on. clean_body: Hi Peter, I don’t know about you, but I spent much of this weekend growing increasingly concerned about what we’re learning about the unregulated expansion of AI in this country and the terrifying claims made by a whistleblower last week, and We now know that AI could pose a real risk to human existence. (Yes, it is as serious as it sounds). And that regulation is needed, and urgently. I’m still learning as much as I can, but I wanted to share some initial thoughts: 1. Our own Senator Sanders is the leading voice on this issue right now. I agree with what he is calling for: encourage international cooperation, call on Congress to act immediately, and hit the brakes on advanced AI development and artificial superintelligence. 2. Even here in Vermont we can’t sit back, we have to act. We have to get ahead of this potential catastrophe. Here’s what we can do: Encourage Governor Phil Scott to work with governors across the country to build a bipartisan coalition calling for urgent, responsible regulation of advanced AI across the country. If you share these concerns, call the Governor’s office at (802) 828-3333. Commit to a moratorium on building any large-scale AI data centers in Vermont while we determine the right path forward, and prepare to re-introduce and consider the Vermont Legislature returns to session. * Make sure our communities have a voice in how this technology develops. You can contact our federal delegation and your local elected officials. Keep asking questions. Keep talking about this. Public engagement matters, especially when technology is moving faster than our laws and institutions. I want to hear from you, too. If you have concerns or ideas about how Vermont should approach AI, I’d be grateful to hear them. I’m not against innovation or economic growth. But Vermont cannot wait and hope for the best. We can welcome innovation while making sure it works for Vermonters. As Lieutenant Governor, I will work with our Congressional delegation, Governor, and Legislature to make sure Vermont is prepared for this rapidly changing industry, that our communities have a voice, and that we protect the resources Vermonters depend on. That’s the kind of leadership I’m ready to bring back to the Lieutenant Governor’s office. AI is moving fast. We can’t afford to wait. Keep those two passages open, and gas stays affordable. Close them both, and the price of nearly everything starts climbing, because oil, diesel, plastics, and fertilizer all move through those waters. A retired Navy officer explained this week that when he left the service in 2024, both straits closing at once was the Pentagon's worst-case scenario for the entire region. **Under Trump's illegal war and Pete Hegseth's Pentagon, it took less than six months to come true.**

clean_body: A combat aviator explains what just happened in the Gulf. | | Peter, Today's message runs longer than usual because I want to walk you through, step by step, how Pete Hegseth turned the Pentagon's worst nightmare into this week's news. I spent 20 years in the Air Force and flew combat missions in the Middle East. Everyone who served understands the whole region sits on a knife's edge. It takes serious, disciplined leadership to keep it from tipping. Unfortunately, this year has proven that Pete Hegseth has none of those qualities. Most of the world's oil travels by ship, and nearly all of it from the Middle East has to squeeze through two narrow waterways (Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb Strait) to reach the rest of us. Keep those two passages open, and gas stays affordable. Close them both, and the price of nearly everything starts climbing, because oil, diesel, plastics, and fertilizer all move through those waters. A retired Navy officer explained this week that when he left the service in 2024, both straits closing at once was the Pentagon's worst-case scenario for the entire region. Under Trump's illegal war and Pete Hegseth's Pentagon, it took less than six months to come true. | Trump's war with Iran already made the Strait of Hormuz too dangerous for shipping, so Saudi Arabia was moving its oil through a backup pipeline to the Red Sea instead. This week, drones launched by Iran's allies blew that pipeline apart. Days later, Iran-backed Houthi fighters seized the Yemeni coastline that controls the Bab el-Mandeb. Both exits are now shut. Oil has shot past $100 a barrel, and everything that travels by truck will cost more. If this course holds, a lot more people are going to die, including Americans in uniform. Meanwhile, this administration is lying to your face about all of it. Trump claims your high gas prices are Ukraine's fault for striking oil refineries inside Russia. That is a blatant lie, and worse, it is Kremlin propaganda, an insult to this country and to the people fighting for their survival against Putin. Keith Self voted for every step of this catastrophe. Even now he cannot find the backbone to say one word against the man who caused it. His silence is a choice, and this district is paying for it at the pump. name: Brian Lenney
subject: We’re NOT the same...
body:
A country is more than an economy with a flag flying over it...

| |
---|---|---
|
# We're NOT the same...
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Sep 14
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
A country is more than an economy with a flag flying over it...
It's a people. A secure border and a language we share. A way of life handed down by the men and women who came through this country on the Oregon Trail and stayed to build the towns we live in now.
Borders, language, culture.
Take those away and the nation is gone.
That is where most of my work sits. English in our schools and our public business. Immigration laws with teeth. Keeping the state out of the way of what Idaho parents are trying to raise their kids to believe.
Libertarianism has nothing to offer on any of it.
Pushed to its honest conclusion, it has something to say against it: a culture is only a preference, a border is only a cage, and no man may tell another man anything past his own property line.
Don't take my word for it.
The Idaho Freedom Foundation's "Freedom Index Analyst" is as Libertarian as they come, and what he put out publicly, under his own name, is genuinely shocking:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a980f535-e951-4c94-a1dc-c2ccc8398edb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That is libertarianism, stated plainly and honestly.
_**We are NOT the same.**_
Their website says the organization exists to "advance the conservative principles," but the guy writing their bill scorecard is publicly arguing for the dissolution of the very things conservatism exists to conserve.
So the next time somebody waves an index number in front of you, know exactly what it measures.
And if that really is the kind of place he wants to live, I hear the South Side of Chicago, Los Angeles, and Memphis are lovely this time of year. No moralistic busybodies. No Karens. No war on drugs, and plenty of cracked-out teenagers waving guns around.
Everything on his list, available today, no legislation required. He just has to leave Idaho to get it.
Idaho isn't signing up for it.
I'll keep voting for the border, the language, and the culture that built this state.
(C) 2026 Brian Lenney

| | | I want to make sure you understand exactly what Donald Trump just proposed, because when you say it plainly, it sounds like a crime — because it basically is one.
At the MAGA midterm convention, Trump promised every American adult a $5,000 check. But read the fine print: He said it would happen if Republicans keep control of the House and Senate in November.
_**The President of the United States is dangling a $5,000 payment in exchange for how you vote. That is not an economic policy. That is a bribe, dressed up as a "dividend."**_
Even Speaker Mike Johnson admitted this wild promise would need actual congressional approval — meaning Trump made a trillion-dollar pledge on a convention stage with zero plan, zero funding mechanism, and zero authority to actually deliver it. His own team can't agree on how to pay for it, whether Congress needs to sign off, or where the $1.3 trillion is supposed to come from. The best answer so far: tariffs.
While Americans are debating a check that will almost certainly never arrive, Trump's DOJ is still sitting on the Epstein files. His war with Iran keeps escalating with no strategy and no end in sight, driving up gas prices along the way. Real, urgent crises — and instead we're talking about a campaign-trail promise designed to grab headlines and change the subject.
**We are not falling for it.**
Equal Opportunity Now isn't distracted by shiny objects and empty promises. We are laser-focused on one thing: electing Democrats who will defeat MAGA extremism in November, no matter what gimmick, distraction, or bribe Donald Trump dangles in front of the country between now and then.

A federal whistle-blower just handed Senators Chuck Schumer and Alex Padilla a nearly 30-page account of something called the "Unlawful Voter Initiative" — **a Homeland Security operation that has deployed hundreds of federal agents to comb through voter rolls managed by states like mine.** According to the whistle-blower, agents were directed by top Homeland Security leaders to use private information to look up voter records — **_and some of them may have broken state laws doing it. _** Agents allegedly posed as voters. They were handed quotas that gave them **12 minutes** to review each voter record. And the whole thing was built on questionable data that likely flagged U.S. citizens who are perfectly eligible to vote.**Twelve minutes.** That's how long the federal government is spending before it decides whether your right to vote is legitimate. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. Protecting the voter roll in this state is my job — not the job of federal agents working off bad data to hit a quota set in Washington.** This was never about fraud. It's about building a pretext — so that when the results come in this fall, Donald Trump has something to point to that allows him to undermine the results. Oregon runs the most accessible and fair election system in America. I intend to keep it that way, and I intend to fight anyone who tries to intimidate an Oregon voter off our rolls. But I can't do that without people willing to back this office up. **[So can you chip in $15 right now so I can continue talking to voters around the state and explaining to them the stakes of this election? clean_body: | | | = | | | I need you to read what came out this morning. = A federal whistle-blower just handed Senators Chuck Schumer and Alex Padilla a nearly 30-page account of something called the "Unlawful Voter Initiative" — a Homeland Security operation that has deployed hundreds of federal agents to comb through voter rolls managed by states like mine. According to the whistle-blower, agents were directed by top Homeland Security leaders to use private information to look up voter records — and some of them may have broken state laws doing it. Agents allegedly posed as voters. They were handed quotas that gave them 12 minutes to review each voter record. And the whole thing was built on questionable data that likely flagged U.S. citizens who are perfectly eligible to vote.Twelve minutes. That's how long the federal government is spending before it decides whether your right to vote is legitimate. I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. Protecting the voter roll in this state is my job — not the job of federal agents working off bad data to hit a quota set in Washington. This was never about fraud. It's about building a pretext — so that when the results come in this fall, Donald Trump has something to point to that allows him to undermine the results. Oregon runs the most accessible and fair election system in America. I intend to keep it that way, and I intend to fight anyone who tries to intimidate an Oregon voter off our rolls. But I can't do that without people willing to back this office up. = = They're counting on us being too distracted to notice. Let's prove them wrong.Thank you,Tobias Read Oregon Secretary of State | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Friends of Tobias Read (5208) PO Box 42307 Portland, OR 97242 United States If you believe you received this message in error or wish to no longer receive email from us, please .

Young Trump voters powered his path back to the White House — and he betrayed them. Now they need a vision for the future they can trust.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260914-1&t=1&akid=4011%2E587540%2EErNnEV)
Peter,
In a minute, **[I’m going to ask you to pitch in $5 to help us hit our midmonth fundraising goal so our candidates have the resources they need to carry on their fight through the midterms.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260914_1_buyers.sEhvuT&refcode=em20260914-4011&amount=5&t=2&akid=4011%2E587540%2EErNnEV)**
But first, I want to talk to you about the opportunity sitting right in front of us this November — and it’s bigger than we may realize.
Earlier this year, _Washington Post_ ran a piece about young people who voted for Trump in 2024.
What they found was a growing sense from these voters that they had been misled and left behind. Polls are saying that 70% of Americans aged 18 to 29 disapprove of Trump’s presidency.
The message is clear: **they’re having buyer's remorse.**
The young voters who helped catapult Trump back to the White House are furious about him waging an endless war in Iran, furious about the devastatingly high prices that never came down, and furious that they were so brazenly lied to.
But here’s the thing. These young voters who feel betrayed by the vision they were sold don’t automatically start showing up for us. They need a reason. They need bold, fearless candidates who can actually relate to what they’re going through. The cost of rent, access to health care, crushing student debt. **They need a vision for the future worth fighting for — and more importantly, one they can trust.**
That’s the work. And with 50 days left until the midterms, the window to do it is right now.
It’s exactly what Leaders We Deserve was built to do. We’re backing and electing candidates in red-to-blue races across the country who are fiercely committed to fighting for the communities they come from, and refuse to take corporate cash or special interest money. These leaders are proving that working class politics can win _anywhere_.
But those victories cost money.
Our ability to support these candidates comes entirely from grassroots supporters like you. Together, we can build a Democratic Party we're proud of that earns the youth vote for the long term, not by just talking about young people's problems, but by actually delivering tangible solutions.
That’s why we really need your support right now to elect **the next generation of courageous fighters who can turn that buyer’s remorse into a mandate for change.**
**[So Peter, will you make a $5 contribution toward our mid-month goal before midnight tomorrow?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260914_1_buyers.sEhvuT&refcode=em20260914-4011&amount=5&t=3&akid=4011%2E587540%2EErNnEV)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Peter,

We wanted to share a harrowing anecdote from one of our recent candidate interviews.

But first, some background:
Florida has one of the strictest abortion laws in the nation. They currently have a 6-week abortion ban with incredibly narrow exceptions, a mandatory waiting period of 24 hours, and a requirement to attend an in-person consultation. State law also requires notarized parental consent for minors, **except when a minor obtains a judicial bypass.**

Lindsay Polega-Quigley is running for the Florida House of Representatives. But before she was a candidate running for office, she was a pro bono attorney supporting those minors (girls 17 years old and **__younger__**) as they were forced to appear before a court and make the case to a judge that they were “mature enough” to make the decision to have an abortion.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139202914/646566263/-1996850302?refcode=EM_F_260914minors_N_BZ_IN-NO_8_G_N_P1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg4NDk1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjZhYmM2NmE5LTg3YjAtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWYxZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=Bd4hHoT_qg56SC0sq84DR3yqeXqCv_SZgJedjIcgbuI=)
---
Lindsay advocated for these girls in court at least once a week. But ever since Florida’s 6-week abortion ban went into effect in 2023, nearly all of her pro bono clients’ requests were rejected because their pregnancies were too far along – even at 6 weeks + 1 day. **That means these very young girls would be forced to carry their pregnancies to term or attempt to travel to another state thousands of miles away.** That’s just one of the reasons Lindsay decided to run for office – because these laws were so draconian, she could no longer make a meaningful difference in the courtroom.

While Lindsay has spent her career fighting insurance companies on behalf of families who had lost everything, protecting reproductive rights, and creating opportunities for young women, her opponent is an anti-choice real estate mogul handpicked by the GOP. We need to help Lindsay win her race and bring her advocacy to the halls of power in Florida.

This is a competitive open seat in a generally blue district. **Republicans are spending _millions_ in an attempt to flip it red, and Lindsay needs our support to win.**

Hey folks,
Mitch McConnell was supposed to return to the Senate. He didn't show up.
After more than three months out of public view, his staff still won't give the American people straight answers--and almost everyone in Washington seems content to move on. I'm not. Because this is bigger than Mitch McConnell. It's about transparency, accountability, gerontocracy, and a political system that protects its own.

* [**00:02:47**] Why does nobody in Congress seem willing to demand real answers?

This episode gets at the heart of why we're building Endless Urgency. A sitting senator can disappear from public view for months, his staff can dodge basic questions, and Washington can keep functioning like the public isn't entitled to answers. Whether we're talking about McConnell, the Epstein files, Trump's health, corruption, or any other story powerful people would prefer disappear, our job is to stay on it. To ask. To investigate. Alright, Derek – let’s walk through this together:
Growing up, my family faced challenges that many Wisconsinites know all too well, including addiction, mental health challenges, and unstable housing. I never knew if I would come home to find our belongings on the curb from another eviction, food in the refrigerator, or a safe place to land. My parents worked hard, but it was tough.
**Luckily, I had people in my community who believed in me and gave me opportunities that changed my life.**
They helped me graduate from high school, supported my passion for public service, and helped me run for elected office. They also helped me return to college to finish my undergraduate degree while serving as Milwaukee County executive.
I’ve had an unconventional path, Derek, but my community has had my back every step of the way. **I believe every person, every family deserves that same support.**
That belief shaped my priorities as Milwaukee County executive, and it’s why I’m running for governor now. I’ve seen first-hand what happens when we put working families first:
→ When we expanded access to affordable housing, **our per capita unhoused population dropped to _the lowest in the nation_**. Now, fewer families suffer the upheaval of eviction that my family faced.
→ When we expanded healthcare access – including opening a 24/7 walk-in mental health emergency center – **our community felt the relief of _safe, comprehensive care close to home_**. That’s a resource I wish my parents would've had.
→ When we invested in public transit and local parks, **our communities thrived with new opportunities to stay connected and active.** Now, folks from backgrounds like mine have greater access to the kinds of opportunities that helped me thrive.
**But, Derek, this is just the beginning.**
I’m serious about fighting to make life better for working families across Wisconsin. I’m serious about lowering costs, funding our public schools, expanding access to healthcare and public services. I’m serious about building a Wisconsin where working people can build a life they love without leaving the state they love.
**So, Derek, my cards are on the table. You’ve seen my track record, and you’ve heard my vision for the future of Wisconsin. clean_body: I’m laying all my cards on the table so you can see my track record for yourself. | | | | During the next 50 days of this campaign, you’ll hear me talk a lot about how my working-class background shapes my vision for Wisconsin’s future. That’s not just a talking point, Derek. It’s how I govern. But I won’t ask you to take my word for it. Today, I want to lay all my cards on the table so you can see my track record for yourself. This is a longer email than I usually send, and I really hope you’ll stick around to hear my story. | | Alright, Derek – let’s walk through this together: Growing up, my family faced challenges that many Wisconsinites know all too well, including addiction, mental health challenges, and unstable housing. I never knew if I would come home to find our belongings on the curb from another eviction, food in the refrigerator, or a safe place to land. My parents worked hard, but it was tough. Luckily, I had people in my community who believed in me and gave me opportunities that changed my life. They helped me graduate from high school, supported my passion for public service, and helped me run for elected office. They also helped me return to college to finish my undergraduate degree while serving as Milwaukee County executive. I’ve had an unconventional path, Derek, but my community has had my back every step of the way. I believe every person, every family deserves that same support. That belief shaped my priorities as Milwaukee County executive, and it’s why I’m running for governor now. I’ve seen first-hand what happens when we put working families first: → When we expanded access to affordable housing, our per capita unhoused population dropped to the lowest in the nation. Now, fewer families suffer the upheaval of eviction that my family faced. → When we expanded healthcare access – including opening a 24/7 walk-in mental health emergency center – our community felt the relief of safe, comprehensive care close to home. That’s a resource I wish my parents would've had. → When we invested in public transit and local parks, our communities thrived with new opportunities to stay connected and active. Now, folks from backgrounds like mine have greater access to the kinds of opportunities that helped me thrive. But, Derek, this is just the beginning. I’m serious about fighting to make life better for working families across Wisconsin. I’m serious about lowering costs, funding our public schools, expanding access to healthcare and public services. I’m serious about building a Wisconsin where working people can build a life they love without leaving the state they love. So, Derek, my cards are on the table. You’ve seen my track record, and you’ve heard my vision for the future of Wisconsin. Now, I’m asking you to stand with me to make it a reality. body:
The dubbed “Stop Nick Shirley Act” was made to stop me.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e11547081/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvRm1lNmN4a01tbQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA5MTQ/LbmNseWdCU1IxNA/qP2hpZHM9bmMwWnJTM1JHY0JYNnhscw/gaqhzow/s1l488f40c3)

# Patriot,
---
There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the **"Stop Nick Shirley Act"** means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law _actually_ does.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Patriot: **it makes it harder for anyone — me included — to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent.** I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; _this is just the beginning._ Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. **The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General** — the _one person_ in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Patriot. That's the system protecting itself. **[Patriot, will you make a tax-deductible gift of $25, $50, or $100 today to help keep independent journalists like me in the field?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Yes —****I'll****Help Keep Independent Journalists in the Field** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't — daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ — and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Patriot: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, **Lincoln Media Foundation** was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. _That’s why I’m partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation._ They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the _first place._ I’m grateful for their partnership and commitment, and **[every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** – helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

**Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible** , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer.
---
[ **Yes —****I'll****Fund Independent Investigations** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Patriot, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that’s why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech — and that’s why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! **[Will you help LMF keep me — and journalists like me — in the field with a gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can give today?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
For the truth,

_**Nick Shirley**_
---
[ **Help Support Nick’s Work** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
P.S. — A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. That tells you how serious this is. **[A tax-deductible gift today helps LMF keep me and other independent journalists in the field while this fight plays out.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**

We hope to have you on our team, but if you want to unsubscribe, [click here](https://secure.ngpvan.com/p/amUvV7y1OUuv63ZcQ0rAzg2?unsubscribedata=EI9S2qokTLmjBgkjAjC%2FDAuncMdyWQq6t2uBZKsTeO%2FXgGK%2F1GowHknqYI%2BXjgFxUOTQiRgYxyvvWxmEPFgMVgtteDx7YdkPorhkVg%2B2411PFpVP48gUtSiJY6n2WN71m5GvujUdxOrz%2FJ%2FSGqiDmqhYDxj6vcLLk4yiWY%2F4F9oJpgh6eZ3X%2Fr3TEiwDXX%2BPnHWBSeIrOnb2a%2BwZBIPgNLA20uMBIRF2IEy08YpqBuKWMq7Fa26Bh2i5GQemcZ5%2FMT195hpew55VVzwhlOr33DnLKGYNYHIKYQnU%2FpHkiTRJqGo8lw3bFUeyWhIXxIvKMk54gjZK6CPaQflFVVvqO5Iote0wQ1R4UB7V%2BxOEKL%2F5aO15hJdxBoWRpV0ugQCt3PvE6%2B5j7HUqVFRLB%2F6oOE1GNmVEPSHhtfwxLp6RsUjPY4i438d3c40FGOE7TjJD).

Peter, A few weeks ago, I visited Dilley Trailer Prison in Texas, the only ICE detention center in the country for families, and it was absolutely **gut-wrenching.** **No one in this center has a criminal record of any kind, and yet they are facing unfathomable trauma, uncertainty, and fear while here.** I spoke to a number of individuals, including a 16-year-old and her father. She was on her way to church when ICE took her, and then lured her father as well. _“I’ve never committed a crime,” he told me. “I have no criminal record.”_ I am beyond relieved that, after our oversight visit, they were released. Peter, stories like these are far too common under this administration. **We need to keep raising our voices, calling out this abuse, and stop letting ICE get away with It.** **Dilley needs to be shut down.** **I’m devastated and outraged, but determined.** Our taxpayer dollars are being used to _hurt children_ , separate families, and push Donald Trump’s corrupt agenda. [**We must ensure a blue wave this November to elect Democrats who will shut Dilley down and help end this horrific practice. Dan dodged debate invitations for months and said he would only participate if it was in his interest. But we were too loud for him to ignore.
Because we came together and demanded to be heard, he'll have to face the voters and answer for his record next month.
**And if we keep this up, he 'll be held accountable at the ballot box in 50 days.**
Our part of PA is done being pushed to the side by our do-nothing congressman. We're proving over and over again that we have the power to make real change. Now we need to take this momentum and run with it.
**Over the next 50 days, we have to knock every door we can, get our ads on the screens of every undecided voter, and make sure everyone in our part of PA knows what we 're fighting for. But we need the resources to get it done.**
**[With 50 days to go, can you chip in to power us through this final stretch?](https://substack.com/redirect/90f00906-1e44-4a1c-9e9c-ca6d7862ce22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you to everyone who spoke up and made this happen. Let's keep our foot on the gas and win this thing.
- Rachel Wallace

**Good news:** Abbott and I are tied in the polls _right now._
No one has come this close. We can win this fall.

Peter, it's Dinesh D'Souza.

I want to share something deeply personal with you today. Something I've never said quite this way before.

**The night before I was set to be locked away, I made a decision that changed everything about how I fight and how I've fought ever since.**

I'm not going to bury the lead: _**what I learned in that moment is the same thing I believe every patriot in this movement needs to hear right now. **_

As an instructor in Georgia State’s nursing school, I’ve spent years teaching and supporting the students who keep our healthcare system alive. I know how hard they work, how much they sacrifice, and how urgently our state needs more advanced practice nurses — not fewer.
So when I saw this headline...
https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
...I felt sick.
Under Donald Trump’s new proposal, advanced nursing degrees would no longer count as “professional,” meaning students would lose access to the federal loans they need to pursue graduate education. Loan limits would be slashed in half. Thousands of future nurse practitioners, nurse midwives, CRNAs, and clinical nurse specialists could be forced to take on massive private debt — or give up their dreams entirely.
This is not just bad policy.
It’s dangerous — for patients, for hospitals, and for the future of healthcare in this country.
Georgia already faces provider shortages. Rural communities already wait weeks for care. And now Trump wants to create even fewer advanced practice nurses?
We cannot allow this to go unanswered.
The American Nurses Association has already sounded the alarm, and more than 200,000 nurses and patients have raised their voices. Now I’m asking you to add yours:
Will you sign the petition demanding the Department of Education reverse this reckless decision and recognize advanced nursing degrees as the professional degrees they are? [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/4OI02pK92kOTd_uWTjBgFg2]
Our nurses deserve respect. Our students deserve opportunity. And our healthcare system deserves investment — not sabotage.
Thank you for standing up for science, for students, and for the people who keep us healthy.
